item.title: US stocks: Nasdaq ends down as chipmakers fall and bank earnings roll in
item.description: In a recent trading session, the Nasdaq index took a hit as chip stocks continued their downward spiral, amid diverging results from major banks like Citigroup and Goldman Sachs. The PHLX chip index faced a substantial decline, sparking fears surrounding competition in this sector. Despite the turbulence, analysts express optimism about future earnings linked to AI-driven innovations.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Nasdaq ended lower on Tuesday, as chip stocks added to recent losses and investors parsed mixed quarterly results from Citigroup and other big US banks.The PHLX chip index fell for a fifth straight session, after Broadcom CEO Hock Tan on Monday likened some of the investment flow into the sector to casino gambling. Additionally, reports of technological advances by Chinese memory chip company CXMT underscored concerns about rising competition.Micron Technology and Applied Materials both fell sharply. Broadcom rose.Citigroup dipped and Goldman Sachs rose after both banks topped profit estimates.Wells Fargo fell after its net interest income missed estimates, while JPMorgan Chase swung between gains and losses following a rare profit miss.Apple hit an intraday record high.Analysts on average see S&P 500 third-quarter earnings surging over 30%, fueled largely by AI-related technology companies, according to LSEG data.Expectations of a strong earnings season have offset worries about the US war with Iran, surging bond yields and inflation related to high oil prices.Also Read | NY Fed President Williams sees no need for a rate hike in 2027 A lot of investors are feeling a sense of relief that markets might start looking at earnings and less at the bond market, less at higher-for-longer oil prices and less at high interest rates, said Jake Dollarhide, CEO of Longbow Asset Management in Tulsa, Oklahoma.According to preliminary data, the S&P 500 lost 1.41 points, or 0.02%, to end at 7,805.83 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 42.37 points, or 0.15%, to 27,203.53. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 173.10 points, or 0.33%, to 51,677.45.The S&P 500 has rallied about 14% in 2026, lifted by AI-related technology stocks. However, the median stock in the index is up less than 5% and over 200 S&P 500 components are down for the year.Reflecting expectations of strong corporate earnings from AI heavyweights, the S&P 500 is trading at under 19 times expected earnings, its lowest since 2023.The PHLX chip index has lost more than 8% in the past five sessions and it remains up over 70% year-to-date.The S&P 500 healthcare index fell on Tuesday, with Johnson & Johnson down despite topping profit estimates.Bumble jumped after the dating-app operator agreed to go private in a $1.3 billion deal.Domino's Pizza declined after scaling back its full-year sales outlook.

item.title: Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua bout could start after 1 a.m. in Wales
item.description: A request to hold the much-anticipated heavyweight bout between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua in the very early morning hours has been filed in Cardiff, Wales.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A request to hold the much-anticipated heavyweight bout between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua in the very early morning hours has been filed in Cardiff, Wales. If approved, the bout would have a ring walk of 1 a.m. local time on Dec. 12, which equates to 8 p.m. on the East Coast of the United States and 5 p.m. on the West Coast on Dec. 11. The 74,000-seat Principality Stadium, home to the Wales national rugby team, is set to host the bout. Both Fury and Joshua have different stipulations as to where the bout can take place, with Cardiff working out as a compromise after locations like Dublin, Las Vegas and New York also were considered, The Athletic reported. Fury, 38, is from Manchester, England, while Joshua, 36, is from Watford, Hertfordshire, England. Cardiff requires boxing and wrestling events to end by 1 a.m., with the request asking for an extension until 3 a.m., with the stadium open until 3:30 a.m. A request to serve alcohol into the early-morning hours also has been submitted. Netflix is set to broadcast the bout, which was announced in September. Elected officials, as well as members of the public, have until Nov. 3 to give their opinion on the time extension to the Cardiff Council. --Field Level Media

item.title: Federal Circuit rejects PTAB's 'ministerial' requirement for prior art priority
item.description: Jonathan Bowser of Haynes Boone discusses the Federal Circuit's rejection of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board's "ministerial" standard for determining when a prior art patent can claim an earlier filing date under the America Invents Act.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Bowser
item.content:encoded: A backdating Issue The scenario recurs often. An inter partes review petitioner wants to use a patent or published application as prior art, but the reference's own filing date is too late. The reference, however, claims priority to a provisional or parent application filed before the challenged patent's effective filing date. If the reference can reach back to that earlier date, it becomes prior art. If it cannot, the petitioner's invalidity ground collapses. Patent claims are governed under the AIA if they have an effective filing date on or after March 16, 2013. Patent claims with an effective filing date before March 16, 2013, are governed under pre-AIA law. Under pre-AIA law, the requirement for proving a reference patent is entitled to the earlier date of its provisional is governed by the Federal Circuit's decision in Dynamic Drinkware, LLC v. National Graphics, Inc., 800 F.3d 1375 (Fed. Cir. 2015). Under Dynamic Drinkware, a reference patent is entitled to its provisional's date only if (1) the provisional provides written description support under 35 U.S.C. § 112 for at least one claim of the reference patent, and (2) the subject matter relied upon in the reference patent is described in the provisional. The rationale was straightforward. A challenger should not be able to backdate prior art by claiming priority from an application that would not itself have supported a patent on the claimed invention. The Board's Penumbra framework In Penumbra, Inc. v. RapidPulse, Inc., IPR2021-01466, 2023 WL 2605070 (P.T.A.B. March 10, 2023), the Board held that Dynamic Drinkware's claim-support requirement was a product of pre-AIA § 102(e) and does not govern prior art determinations under AIA § 102. Instead, the Board announced a two-part test. A reference patent need only satisfy the "ministerial requirements" of AIA §§ 119 and 120 — a proper benefit claim, co-pendency, common inventorship — and the earlier application must "describe the subject matter" relied upon in the reference as prior art. Whether any claim of the reference was actually entitled to priority, the Board said, is not at issue. That framework did not emerge from nowhere. The Board leaned on the AIA's structural distinction between the "effective filing date" of a claimed invention under § 100(i) and the date a reference is "effectively filed" for prior art purposes under § 102(d). It also relied heavily on USPTO guidance, including MPEP § 2154.01(b) and a 2018 memorandum to the examining corps stating that the Dynamic Drinkware claim-support requirement "is not applicable when examining an application subject to the first inventor to file provisions of the AIA." Penumbra was designated precedential, and the Board applied it routinely — including in the IPR on appeal in Dental Monitoring, where the Board treated the reference patent as prior art as of its provisional date without deciding whether the provisional described any of the reference patent's claims. The statute supplies the answer The Federal Circuit based its decision in Dental Monitoring SAS v. Align Technology, Inc., 184 F.4th 1376 (Fed. Cir. 2026), on the text of the AIA. Section 102(d)(2) gives a reference the benefit of an earlier filing date only "if the patent or application for patent is entitled to claim a right of priority under [§] 119." Section 119(e)(1), in turn, extends entitlement to provisional priority only where the invention is "disclosed [in the provisional] in the manner provided by [§] 112(a)." Section 102(d) therefore incorporates a substantive written description requirement, and nothing in its text carves out prior art determinations or supplies a "less demanding 'ministerial' standard." The Court placed particular weight on the words "entitled to claim." That phrasing, it explained, refers to substantive entitlement, not the procedural act of asserting priority. Congress could have written § 102(d)(2) to cover a patent that merely "claims" or "asserts" a right of priority. It did not, and reading the provision the Board's way would render "entitled to" superfluous. The Court also corrected a persistent misreading of Dynamic Drinkware. Align argued that the decision was confined to pre-AIA § 102(e). But Dynamic Drinkware's footnote declining to address "newly designated § 102(d)" was a reservation of decision, not a holding that the AIA abrogated the written description requirement. The court noted that Align "confuses a reservation of decision with a holding on the merits." Even assuming Dynamic Drinkware does not formally control, the underlying principle survives: a reference cannot obtain the benefit of an earlier filing date for subject matter the earlier application did not support. As for § 100(i), the Court agreed that the AIA distinguishes an invention's effective filing date from a reference's effective prior art date, but held that the distinction "identifies which statutory inquiry is being performed" without telling us what substantive requirements "entitled" incorporates. And the Board's statements describing § 102(d) as imposing only "ministerial" requirements could not carry the day, because "the authoritative statement is the statutory text, not the legislative history." Because the Board never made the necessary factual findings, the court vacated and remanded rather than reversing, leaving the written description question for the Board in the first instance. A word on Rule 36 Practitioners who had treated Penumbra as blessed by the Federal Circuit should note a pointed footnote. The Court had earlier affirmed Penumbra by Rule 36 judgment without opinion.RapidPulse, Inc. v. Penumbra Inc., Nos. 2024-1130 and 2024-1131, 2025 WL 2911056 (Oct. 14, 2025). That affirmance, the Court explained, establishes only that the judgment below was correct; it "does not endorse or reject any specific part of the [Board's] reasoning," and "has no precedential value." A Rule 36 win is not an endorsement of the reasoning that produced it. Takeaways Petitioners bear a new burden of proof for prior art reference patents challenging AIA patents. Any ground resting on a reference patent's provisional or parent filing date now requires an affirmative showing that the earlier application provides § 112(a) written description support for at least one of the reference's published claims. That is a claim-by-claim, four-corners analysis — not a citation to the benefit claim on the reference's face. Petitions should build that record up front, with expert support, because the petitioner has the burden of persuasion to establish that a reference patent qualifies as prior art. Patent owners gain a powerful gatekeeping argument. Where the petition is silent on claim support, patent owners can attack the reference's prior art status directly, without engaging the merits of the obviousness theory. In closely spaced priority contests, that argument may be dispositive. Finally, the decision is a reminder about the durability of PTAB precedent. A precedential PTAB decision built substantially on agency guidance and legislative history is vulnerable when the statutory text points the other way — and a Rule 36 affirmance will not insulate it. This article reflects only the present personal considerations, opinions, and/or views of the author, which should not be attributed to the author's current or prior law firm(s) or former or present clients. Jonathan Bowser is a regular contributing columnist on patent law for Reuters Legal News and Westlaw Today.

item.title: Glencore shares to start trading in Australia as miner hopes to boost valuation
item.description: Glencore's , shares are set to start trading on the Australian Securities Exchange on Wednesday as the miner and trader hopes to secure a better valuation from Australia's mining-friendly investors who are seeking greater exposure to copper.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Glencore's (GLEN.L) , shares are set to start trading on the Australian Securities Exchange on Wednesday as the miner and trader hopes to secure a better valuation from Australia's mining-friendly investors who are seeking greater exposure to copper. Glencore CEO Gary Nagle expects strong demand from investors betting on copper's role in [USN:L8N45U2BV TEXT:"electrification"], he said on Friday, as demand rises for the metal's use in power grid upgrades, transport and AI data centres. The Switzerland-based company's CHESS Depository Interests (CDIs) will trade in a market home to other large miners like BHP Group (BHP.AX) , Rio Tinto (RIO.AX) , (RIO.L) and Fortescue (FMG.AX) . Glencore shares already trade in London and Johannesburg. Nagle has previously said he believes the $88 billion company can achieve inclusion in Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index (.AXJO) within 12 months, but analysts see momentum behind the stock potentially propelling it into the top indexes in [USN:L4N3Z11V1 TEXT:"half that time"]. Analysts and investors speculated Glencore's decision to list Down Under could help acclimatise those [USN:L8N44B03D TEXT:"who had not seen value"] in its approach to Rio Tinto last year. Rio Tinto walked away from takeover talks with Glencore in February, ending months of negotiations over a $240 billion tie-up that would have reshaped the global mining industry. Nagle told reporters last week that a deeper local presence in Australia, where it produces coal, copper, zinc, lead and nickel, may [USN:L8N45U2BV TEXT:"yield business opportunities"], although it had no set buyout list. JPMorgan analysts said on Friday after a meeting with Nagle that Glencore's management team still saw merits in a combination with Rio Tinto and noted its shares had outperformed its Anglo-Australian rival by 10% since negotiations collapsed in February. "M&A is seen as part of the growth strategy and it was noted 'who knows what happens in the future,'" the analysts said in a report.

item.title: US Supreme Court denies bid for pretrial release by anti-ICE activist
item.description: The US Supreme Court on Tuesday declined to allow the pretrial release of an anti-ICE activist whose arrest for an allegedly threatening social media post during an immigration crackdown in Minneapolis was touted by President Donald Trump's administration in its campaign against "left-wing agitators."
item.dc:creator: John Kruzel
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court on Tuesday declined to allow the pretrial release of an anti-ICE activist whose arrest for an allegedly threatening social media post during an immigration crackdown in Minneapolis was touted by President Donald Trump 's administration in its campaign against "left-wing agitators." The justices denied self-described antifa, or "anti-fascist," member Kyle Wagner's request to revive a judge's ruling that ordered his pretrial release. Wagner was returned to custody after federal prosecutors appealed the judge's release order, arguing that he posed a danger to the community. Wagner's lawyers argued in court papers that he was being unlawfully detained and noted that he has no violent criminal history. Trump has made countering left-wing groups — and antifa in particular — a priority during his second term in office. The Republican president signed an executive order last year declaring the movement a "domestic terrorist organization" and has threatened to investigate and prosecute those who financially support it. Wagner faces one count each of cyberstalking and transmitting interstate threats for his attempt to publish personal information, or "dox," a prominent online supporter of Trump's hardline immigration policies. Prosecutors cited other social media posts by Wagner — including his statement that the situation in Minneapolis was "kill or be killed" — as evidence of his dangerousness. Wagner's arrest in Minneapolis on February 5 came during the Trump administration's large deployment of federal agents to the region in an immigration crackdown that spurred protests and led to the killing of two US citizens by immigration agents. During a White House briefing that day, then-White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt displayed a printed photograph of a shirtless Wagner — who has tattoos on his face, neck and chest — and described him to reporters as a "domestic terrorist." "As for the left-wing agitators who have been illegally obstructing ICE's immigration efforts, we are not letting that behavior go unnoticed or unpunished," Leavitt said from the White House lectern. "In fact, just today, the Department of Homeland Security arrested this individual. He is a self-proclaimed antifa member who has been threatening, doxing, harassing ICE." In August, the Cincinnati-based 6th US Circuit Court of Appeals granted the Justice Department's request to reverse US District Judge Denise Page Hood's pretrial release order. Wagner's trial is scheduled to begin in January. Judge Whitney Hermandorfer, a Trump appointee, wrote the 6th Circuit's 2-1 ruling that was joined by Judge Alan Norris, an appointee of Republican former President Ronald Reagan. The 6th Circuit ruled that the administration had made an adequate showing of Wagner's dangerousness. In dissent was Judge Rachel Bloomekatz, an appointee of Democratic former President Joe Biden, who wrote that, "The government seldom appeals pretrial release orders, so why is it insistent here?" Bloomekatz continued, "Wagner, who identifies as 'antifa' (anti-fascist) and has large tattoos on his face, neck and chest, looks aggressive in his social media videos, so it is no surprise that the White House press secretary held up a photo from one of his videos while touting law enforcement efforts against 'left-wing agitators.' ... But Wagner has never committed a violent crime." In his Supreme Court filing, Wagner's lawyers told the justices that the 6th Circuit's conclusion about his dangerousness was based on a "tendentious reading of Wagner's social media postings."

item.title: Fed's Collins sees another rate hike on the table before end of 2026
item.description: Boston Federal Reserve President Susan Collins said on Tuesday she believes the US central bank will need to raise interest rates again before the end of this year to lower high inflation.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: Boston Federal Reserve President Susan Collins said on Tuesday she believes the US central bank will need to raise interest rates again before the end of this year to lower high inflation. Collins said she backed the rate hike by the central bank's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee last month and currently expects "it will be appropriate to raise rates a bit further before the end of the year to ensure a timely and durable return of inflation to the Committee's 2% target." "My view of the need for further policy action, and the appropriate timing, will depend importantly on how the totality of incoming data shapes my outlook and the associated balance of risks," she said in the text of a speech to be delivered at a banking conference at the Boston Fed. Collins said that with the economy and job market doing well, the Fed can focus its work on bringing inflation back down to its target after missing that goal for more than five years. The Fed raised its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point to the 3.75%-4.00% range last month. Policymaker forecasts released at that meeting penciled in another increase by the end of 2026, although a range of Fed officials have in recent weeks [USN:S0N44V01O TEXT:"strongly suggested"] the move will come in December and not at the October 27-28 meeting. Collins was largely upbeat about the economic outlook, though she acknowledged there were risks. The "most likely" path "continues to feature healthy GDP growth, with the labor market remaining near full employment," she said. "In this scenario, inflation gradually returns to 2%, as continued efficiency gains support the balance between demand and supply, and contribute to disinflation." But pressure from tech investment to build AI infrastructure and the ongoing impact of tariffs and energy costs driven by the war in the Middle East could complicate the effort to lower inflation, she said. "I expect both total and core inflation to again run above the Fed's 2% target in the coming months, given the recent jump in prices of refined energy products like jet and diesel fuel, and home heating oil," Collins added.

item.title: Saudi OpenAI engineer arrested by FBI over hidden recording device, US DOJ says
item.description: US federal agents arrested a Saudi national employed as an OpenAI engineer and charged him with installing a hidden audio recording device in an executive conference room at the AI company, the Justice Department said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US federal agents arrested a Saudi national employed as an OpenAI engineer and charged him with installing a hidden audio recording device in an executive conference room at the AI company, the Justice Department said on Tuesday. OpenAI had used its internal AI models to identify the individual responsible for planting the device and to trace its origins, it said in an X post . "At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated," according to the AI company. The company said it referred the matter to the FBI, which is continuing to investigate. The FBI did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for more details. Earlier this year, a Texas man [USN:L4N40W1SN TEXT:"was charged with "]throwing a Molotov cocktail at the home of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and attempting to set fire to the AI firm's headquarters. OpenAI faces scrutiny over security incidents involving its AI systems. Reuters and other media outlets reported recently that [USN:L6N45U1FJ TEXT:"the company had told investors"] its annualized revenue for September was almost $50 billion, a drop from what it signaled earlier. OpenAI said on Friday it fired [USN:L6N45V0B0 TEXT:"three researchers "]after an investigation found they had violated company policies on handling sensitive information. The statement came after the researchers, Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni, published a letter detailing the circumstances of their dismissal and arguing that the abrupt firings could create uncertainty among employees and undermine a culture that had allowed researchers to raise safety concerns.

item.title: Uber gets green light to pursue racketeering case against Philadelphia lawyer
item.description: Uber Technologies can pursue civil racketeering claims against a Philadelphia-based lawyer even though the company's insurer footed its defense bills in a series of allegedly fraudulent personal injury lawsuits, a federal judge ruled on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: David Thomas
item.content:encoded: Uber Technologies (UBER.N) can pursue civil racketeering claims against a Philadelphia-based lawyer even though the company's insurer footed its defense bills in a series of allegedly fraudulent personal injury lawsuits, a federal judge ruled on Tuesday. US District Judge Mark Kearney in Philadelphia held that the rideshare giant has standing to pursue its case against Marc Simon and his firm Simon & Simon. Uber alleges the law firm worked with doctors and other providers to file fraudulent personal injury claims against it and Federal Express Corporation (FDX.N) . Simon and his firm have denied wrongdoing. "Uber did not relinquish its standing to sue parties who bring fraudulent claims against it by purchasing liability insurance and permitting its conduit, Farmers, to issue payments on its behalf," Kearney wrote in his 14-page ruling . An Uber spokesperson said in a statement that Kearney's ruling "makes clear that Uber can continue pursuing its racketeering claims, and we remain confident in our case." A spokesperson for Simon & Simon did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The case is scheduled to go to trial in March. Uber and FedEx have mounted similar lawsuits against law firms in federal courts in [USN:L1N3TI014 TEXT:"Los Angeles"], [USN:L6N3SE0TU TEXT:"Miami"] and [USN:L6N40R0DN TEXT:"New York"] alleging lawyers worked in conjunction with medical providers to file bogus and exaggerated claims against them. Kearney in May [USN:L6N41O15M TEXT:"denied a motion to dismiss"] Uber and FedEx's case against the Simon & Simon firm. The companies alleged Simon directs clients to certain providers whose unnecessary treatments or false diagnoses inflate the value of their claims, which could result in a larger settlement. FedEx and Uber claim that Simon and his firm direct these medical providers to create fraudulent documents which are then used as the basis of litigation. Simon has argued that the companies are abusing RICO in an effort to put him out of business. He brought [USN:L6N42H0ZU TEXT:"counterclaims"] against Uber and FedEx in June, asserting their RICO allegations are "objectively and subjectively baseless" because some cases they agreed to settle were being cited as evidence of a racketeering scheme. Kearney dismissed the counterclaims in August.

item.title: Lufthansa set to win bidding for stake in Portugal's TAP, SIC reports
item.description: Germany's Lufthansa is set to win the bidding for the purchase of a 44.9% stake in Portugal's flag carrier TAP over rival Air France-KLM , broadcaster SIC said on Tuesday, citing sources familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Germany's Lufthansa (LHAG.DE) is set to win the bidding for the purchase of a 44.9% stake in Portugal's flag carrier TAP over rival Air France-KLM (AIRF.PA) , broadcaster SIC said on Tuesday, citing sources familiar with the matter. The German group is offering an all-cash deal for its stake in TAP, unlike Air France-KLM, whose proposal combines cash and shares in the Franco-Dutch airline, SIC reported. Lufthansa's stronger financial position was also a key factor, it added. Portugal's Infrastructure Ministry declined to comment. Air France-KLM and Lufthansa submitted final bids for the stake in [USN:L1N44W0H6 TEXT:"September"] after Portugal's government requested both bidders improve their offers. The government is due to choose the winner at an extraordinary cabinet meeting on Wednesday.

item.title: ゼレンスキー氏、米特使との追加協議提案 数日内の会談に意欲
item.description: [１３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[１３日 ロイター] - ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は１３日、米国がウクライナとロシアの交渉再開に向けた取り組みを強化する中、米国のウィットコフ和平交渉担当特使、トランプ米大統領の娘婿ジャレッド・クシュナー氏との新たな協議を数日以内に行うことを提案したと明らかにした。

ゼレンスキー氏の提案は、先週米国で行われた協議を受けたもの。恒例の夜のビデオ演説で「会談や協議に関する提案を米国に送った。われわれは向こう数日以内に会談する用意があり、この提案をウィトコフ氏とクシュナー氏に伝えた」と述べた。トランプ米大統領が発表したエネルギー施設を対象とする停戦については、ロシアが順守する限り支持する考えを改めて示した。

米国、ウクライナ、欧州の交渉担当者は９日、米フロリダ州マイアミで戦争終結に向けた統一提案での合意を目指し、６時間にわたる協議を実施。同日には、トランプ大統領がロシアのプーチン大統領と電話会談を行い、ロシアが米国と世界市場にディーゼル（軽油）を供給することで合意したと発表した。ウィトコフ氏とクシュナー氏はウクライナ代表団に対し、ロシア産ディーゼルの輸出を認める合意は、ロシアを交渉の場に呼び戻すことを目的としていると説明している。

item.title: ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル下落、ＦＲＢ利上げ観測後退 ＣＰＩに注目
item.description: ［ニューヨーク １３日 ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルが円やユーロなどの主要通貨に対し下落した。原油価格...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ外為市場＝ドル下落、ＦＲＢ利上げ観測後退　ＣＰＩに注目 4:55 配信

２０１１年３月撮影　 REUTERS/Kacper Pempel

［ニューヨーク　１３日　ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場では、ドルが円やユーロなどの主要通貨に対し下落した。原油価格の下落や米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）利上げ観測の後退に加え、米国資産の需要を支えてきた人工知能（ＡＩ）に関連した相場上昇を見直す動きが出ていることがドルの重荷になった。

ＦＲＢの今後の利上げの道筋を巡る新たな手掛かりを見極めようとする動きが出る中、ニューヨーク連銀のウィリアムズ総裁が、年内にあと１回の利上げを実施することが適切になるとの見方を変えていないものの、２０２７年に一段の利上げは必要ないとの考えを示したことを受け、ドル相場は一段安となった。

終盤の取引で円は対ドルで０．１８％高の１５８．３３円。日銀が発表した９月の企業物価指数（ＣＧＰＩ）速報によると、国内企業物価指数は前年比６．８％上昇し、国内企業物価指数は前年比６．８％上昇し、ロイターがまとめた民間調査機関の予測中央値の７．６％を下回った。ただ、日銀による一段の金融引き締め観測に加え、急激な為替変動に対する政府・日銀の為替介入への警戒感も引き続き円相場の支援材料になっている。

ユーロは対円で０．１９％高の１７７．２９５円。前日には２５年１１月以来の安値となる１７６．２５円を付けていた。

主要６通貨に対するドル指数は０．３７％安の１０２．１８。前日は１０２．６１まで上昇し、２０２５年４月以来の高水準を付けていた。コーペイ（トロント）のチーフ市場ストラテジスト、カール・シャモッタ氏は「人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株のバリュエーションの強さや持続性に対する懐疑的な見方が強まり、米金融市場への資本流入が鈍るとの見方からドルは下落している」と述べた。

市場ではＦＲＢの今後の金融政策を見極めようと、１４日に発表される９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）が注目されている。ＦＲＢ当局者２人が追加利上げの必要性を判断する前に一段の証拠を見極める必要があるとの考えを示したほか、ウォラーＦＲＢ理事がインフレ期待は「十分に抑制されている」と述べたことを受け、今月の利上げ観測は一段と後退した。

ＣＭＥフェドウオッチによると、２７─２８日の米連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で金利据え置きが決定される確率は約８０％。１カ月前は５１％だった。

終盤の取引でユーロは対ドルで０．４０％高の１．１１９８ドル。前日は１．１１５２５ドルまで下落し、２５年５月以来の安値を付けていた。

item.title: Zelenski busca nuevas conversaciones con enviados de EEUU para poner fin a la guerra con Rusia
item.description: El presidente ucraniano, Volodímir Zelenski, dijo el martes que propuso celebrar nuevas conversaciones en los próximos días con los enviados estadounidenses Steve Witkoff y Jared Kushner, en un momento en que Washington intensifica sus esfuerzos para que Kiev y Moscú vuelvan a la mesa de negociaciones.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente ucraniano, Volodímir Zelenski, dijo el martes que propuso celebrar nuevas conversaciones en los próximos días con los enviados estadounidenses Steve Witkoff y Jared Kushner, en un momento en que Washington intensifica sus esfuerzos para que Kiev y Moscú vuelvan a la mesa de negociaciones. La propuesta surge tras las conversaciones mantenidas la semana pasada en Estados Unidos, en las que Witkoff y Kushner comunicaron a una delegación ucraniana que un acuerdo que permitiera las exportaciones rusas de gasóleo tenía como objetivo hacer que Moscú volviera a la mesa de negociaciones. En su discurso nocturno por video, Zelenski también afirmó que Ucrania apoyaba la tregua energética propuesta por el presidente Donald Trump, siempre y cuando Rusia la respetara. "Nuestro equipo ha enviado a la parte estadounidense las propuestas pertinentes sobre posibles próximas reuniones y conversaciones. En los próximos días, estamos dispuestos a reunirnos y he transmitido esta propuesta a Steve Witkoff y Jared Kushner a través de mi equipo".

item.title: Atlanta Dream to host WNBA Finals Games 3 and 4 at home of NBA's Hawks
item.description: The Atlanta Dream will move Games 3 and 4 of the WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries to the larger home of the NBA's Atlanta Hawks in a bid to accommodate more fans, the Dream and Hawks said in a joint statement on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Atlanta Dream will move Games 3 and 4 of the WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries to the larger home of the NBA's Atlanta Hawks in a bid to accommodate more fans, the Dream and Hawks said in a joint statement on Tuesday. The switch required several scheduling changes because the original date for Game 3 clashed with a concert at the arena, while the Hawks host the Houston Rockets there on the day of Game 4. Game 3 has therefore been brought forward by a day to October 21. Game 4 will still be played on October 24 but with an earlier tip-off so as not to clash with the Hawks game. "This is what the players and the fans deserve," Larry Gottesdiener, Atlanta Dream majority owner, said in a news release. "We are grateful to all of the stakeholders who worked together to resolve the conflicts and make this happen." The Dream, who have played home games in recent seasons at a 3,500-seat venue, announced last week that they would move to the Hawks' arena next year under a multi-year agreement.

item.title: Tears, cheers and long-awaited hugs as USS Abraham Lincoln returns home

item.title: Preços do cacau atingem máxima de um mês por clima adverso ligado ao El Niño
item.description: Os contratos futuros de cacau na ICE atingiram nesta terça-feira seu maior nível em cerca de um mês, em meio a condições climáticas adversas associadas ao El Niño nas principais regiões produtoras, enquanto o açúcar bruto voltou a se aproximar da máxima de 19 meses registrada na semana passada.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros de cacau na ICE atingiram nesta terça-feira seu maior nível em cerca de um mês, em meio a condições climáticas adversas associadas ao El Niño nas principais regiões produtoras, enquanto o açúcar bruto voltou a se aproximar da máxima de 19 meses registrada na semana passada. CACAU * Os contratos futuros de cacau de Londres fecharam com alta de £13, ou 0,3%, a £4.292 por tonelada, após atingirem seu maior patamar desde o início de setembro, a £4.466. * “A Costa do Marfim e o sudoeste de Gana registraram chuvas abaixo do normal (associadas ao El Niño) nos últimos dois meses, e espera-se que esse padrão continue na próxima semana a 10 dias”, afirmou a corretora ADMIS. * O Rabobank afirmou que o clima chuvoso atípico para a época, tanto recente quanto previsto, no Equador — terceiro maior produtor mundial —, também está gerando preocupações quanto à produção. * O contrato de futuros de cacau de Nova York ; subiu 1%, para US$5.733 por tonelada, após atingir seu maior patamar desde meados de setembro, em US$5.965. AÇÚCAR * O contrato de açúcar bruto fechou com alta de 0,26 cent, ou 1,2%, a 21,11 cents por libra-peso, após atingir na última quarta-feira o pico de 19 meses, de 21,24 cents . * “O excesso de chuvas no Brasil (principal produtor) continua a sustentar as estimativas crescentes de cana-de-açúcar a ser deixada sem colheita em 2026, reduzindo a oferta global”, afirmou o Rabobank. * O banco também afirmou que a Índia, segundo maior produtor, pode precisar importar açúcar nesta safra, já que seus estoques estão ficando cada vez mais escassos. * Olhando para o futuro, no entanto, o Rabobank acredita que as chuvas brasileiras deste ano são um bom presságio para a safra do próximo ano e lançam uma perspectiva um tanto pessimista sobre os preços no segundo semestre de 2027. * O Ministério da Agricultura da França reduziu sua previsão de produção de beterraba sacarina para 2026/27 para 25,3 milhões de toneladas, após uma seca no verão, o que representa uma queda de 30% em relação ao ano anterior e o nível mais baixo desde o início dos registros do ministério, em 1980. * O preço do açúcar branco ; subiu 0,2%, para US$561,90 por tonelada. CAFÉ * O contrato de café arábica fechou com alta de 2,1 centavos, ou 0,7%, a US$2,927 por libra-peso. * O ritmo das exportações do Brasil, maior produtor mundial, está mantendo os preços do café sob controle, apesar das preocupações de que o El Niño possa trazer condições de seca no final deste ano, o que prejudicaria a safra de 2027/28. * A Bélgica foi o terceiro maior destino das exportações brasileiras de café em setembro, segundo a associação de exportadores Cecafe, com 344.225 sacas, o que pode significar que parte do café está indo para os armazéns da ICE em Antuérpia. * O contrato de café robusta caiu 0,5%, para US$3.459 por tonelada.

item.title: Soja e milho registram queda com colheita nos EUA em pleno andamento
item.description: Os futuros da soja nos Estados Unidos registraram uma leve queda pela segunda sessão consecutiva nesta terça-feira, à medida que as atividades de colheita ganhavam ritmo em todo o Meio-Oeste após um período de tempo seco e os operadores aguardavam o relatório semanal sobre o andamento da safra após o fechamento do mercado.
item.dc:creator: Karl Plume
item.content:encoded: Os futuros da soja nos Estados Unidos registraram uma leve queda pela segunda sessão consecutiva nesta terça-feira, à medida que as atividades de colheita ganhavam ritmo em todo o Meio-Oeste após um período de tempo seco e os operadores aguardavam o relatório semanal sobre o andamento da safra após o fechamento do mercado. O milho ficou estável ou em queda, com os operadores avaliando o aumento da oferta proveniente de uma colheita intensa no Meio-Oeste contra o aumento da demanda, com os preços próximos às mínimas de dois meses. O trigo registrou ligeira queda, com o mercado ignorando o mais recente ataque a navios na zona de exportação do Mar Negro. O tempo predominantemente seco no Meio-Oeste na última semana permitiu que os agricultores acelerassem a colheita de milho e soja antes das chuvas previstas para as regiões ocidentais no final desta semana, seguidas por um clima mais seco, segundo meteorologistas. “Temos pressão da colheita e o mercado vai aguardar notícias sobre a demanda. Teremos o relatório sobre o andamento da safra mais tarde (terça-feira) e, neste momento, o caminho de menor resistência é a baixa”, disse Craig Turner, consultor de gestão de risco de commodities da StoneX. Analistas consultados pela Reuters esperam, em média, que o Departamento de Agricultura dos EUA informe que 38% da safra de milho do país e 44% da safra de soja já haviam sido colhidos até domingo. A soja com vencimento em novembro na bolsa de Chicago (CBOT) fechou em queda de 4 centavos, a US$12,8375 o bushel, enquanto o milho com vencimento em dezembro registrou queda de 0,25 de centavo, a US$4,8275 o bushel. A retomada da demanda por exportações sustentou os preços do milho depois que o Departamento de Agricultura dos Estados Unidos (USDA) elevou inesperadamente sua previsão de produção dos EUA no final da semana passada, o que fez com que os preços despencassem para as mínimas de dois meses. Os futuros de trigo para dezembro na CBOT caíram 3 centavos, para US$6,6925 por bushel, registrando a quarta queda em cinco pregões. O mercado reagiu pouco à notícia de que dois navios de carga foram atingidos por drones na costa da Bulgária, nos mais recentes ataques à navegação comercial no Mar Negro devido à guerra da Rússia contra a Ucrânia.

item.title: Petróleo fecha sem direção única com perspectiva de mais diesel russo e riscos no Oriente Médio
item.description: Os preços do petróleo fecharam mistos nesta terça-feira, já que as esperanças de que o acordo entre os Estados Unidos e a Rússia sobre o diesel pudesse liberar mais suprimentos de Moscou compensaram os ataques na Arábia Saudita e no Iêmen, que poderiam resultar em novas interrupções no abastecimento.
item.dc:creator: Scott Disavino
item.content:encoded: Os preços do petróleo fecharam mistos nesta terça-feira, já que as esperanças de que o acordo entre os Estados Unidos e a Rússia sobre o diesel pudesse liberar mais suprimentos de Moscou compensaram os ataques na Arábia Saudita e no Iêmen, que poderiam resultar em novas interrupções no abastecimento. Os contratos futuros do Brent fecharam a US$105,69 por barril, uma queda de 0,9%, em relação à segunda-feira, quando o contrato atingiu seu maior fechamento desde 15 de setembro. Os contratos futuros do petróleo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dos Estados Unidos subiram 0,4%, fechando a US$94,14, o maior fechamento do WTI desde 24 de setembro. Os futuros do WTI para o ano civil de 2027 atingiram uma alta recorde pelo 12º dia consecutivo, chegando a US$84 por barril. Na segunda-feira, os futuros do Brent para o ano civil de 2027 atingiram uma alta recorde pelo quarto dia consecutivo, chegando a US$90. O Kremlin afirmou não ver nenhuma ligação direta entre um acordo sobre a exportação de diesel russo para os EUA e a posição de Moscou nas negociações de paz na Ucrânia. O comentário foi feito em resposta a uma reportagem da Reuters baseada em fontes, que informou que enviados do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, haviam dito a autoridades ucranianas na sexta-feira que o acordo para permitir as exportações de diesel russo fazia parte de uma tentativa de trazer a Rússia de volta às negociações sobre um possível acordo de paz na Ucrânia. A Rússia foi o terceiro maior produtor mundial de petróleo, atrás dos EUA e da Arábia Saudita, em 2025, de acordo com dados do setor energético dos EUA. As sanções destinadas a manter a energia russa fora dos mercados globais têm ajudado a sustentar os preços do petróleo desde que a Rússia invadiu a Ucrânia em 2022. Qualquer acordo para encerrar a guerra entre a Rússia e a Ucrânia poderia permitir que a Rússia exportasse mais energia. A Ucrânia não recebeu nenhum aviso dos parceiros ocidentais antes de um ataque com mísseis russos à sua capital, afirmou o presidente Volodymyr Zelenskiy nesta terça-feira. Trump disse que Washington ainda estava compartilhando informações de inteligência, mesmo enquanto pressiona Kiev a interromper os ataques a refinarias russas. Trump afirmou que o diesel russo era destinado ao resto do mundo, não aos EUA. Em um sinal de que o mercado está incerto quanto ao acordo de Trump com a Rússia sobre o diesel, os futuros de diesel dos EUA estavam sendo negociados com alta de cerca de 5% nesta terça-feira. Os preços do diesel atingiram níveis recordes em muitas partes do mundo nas últimas semanas devido a interrupções no abastecimento global relacionadas aos ataques da Ucrânia à infraestrutura energética russa e aos ataques do Irã à infraestrutura energética do Oriente Médio. Por outro lado, o chefe dos serviços de inteligência interna do Reino Unido afirmou nesta terça-feira que a Rússia e o Irã estavam intensificando campanhas de guerra híbrida no Reino Unido.

item.title: CDC enviará reforços à Pensilvânia para investigar surto de sarampo
item.description: O Centro de Controle e Prevenção de Doenças (CDC) dos EUA informou nesta terça-feira que enviará reforços à Pensilvânia para ajudar a investigar o surto de sarampo, já que o Estado solicitou formalmente assistência federal por meio do programa de resposta a emergências Epi-Aid da agência.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Centro de Controle e Prevenção de Doenças (CDC) dos EUA informou nesta terça-feira que enviará reforços à Pensilvânia para ajudar a investigar o surto de sarampo, já que o Estado solicitou formalmente assistência federal por meio do programa de resposta a emergências Epi-Aid da agência. Autoridades de saúde da Pensilvânia registraram 1.136 casos de sarampo e cinco mortes relacionadas ao surto neste ano até 9 de outubro, enquanto o CDC confirmou duas mortes associadas ao sarampo em todo o país em 2026, sem identificar os Estados envolvidos. As diferenças no número de mortes alimentaram uma divergência pública entre o governador da Pensilvânia, Josh Shapiro, e o secretário de Saúde dos EUA, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. -- cujo departamento supervisiona o CDC -- sobre como as mortes associadas ao sarampo devem ser definidas e contabilizadas. A agência afirmou que deve trabalhar com autoridades locais de saúde para investigar o surto, fortalecer os esforços de resposta e impedir a propagação. “O Texas, a Carolina do Sul, a Virgínia, o Kansas, o Novo México e o Wisconsin solicitaram o apoio do programa Epi-Aid do CDC e trabalharam em conjunto com equipes federais para ajudar a controlar seus surtos de forma rápida e bem-sucedida”, afirmou a agência em comunicado. A Reuters havia noticiado com exclusividade em setembro que o departamento de saúde da Pensilvânia solicitou apoio de emergência ao CDC, mas apenas sob a condição de que a agência reconhecesse as mortes associadas ao sarampo relatadas pelo Estado. Separadamente, a governadora de Nova York, Kathy Hochul, afirmou na semana passada que o Estado deve buscar assistência federal para responder ao surto de sarampo, incluindo apoio do Departamento de Saúde e Serviços Humanos dos EUA e do CDC. No entanto, nem o gabinete da governadora nem o Departamento de Saúde do Estado de Nova York esclareceram se um pedido formal foi apresentado. Isso ocorreu após Hochul declarar emergência em todo o Estado devido ao surto, a primeira declaração do tipo por um Estado dos EUA desde o aumento dos casos de sarampo em 2025. Nova York registrou 126 casos de sarampo até 13 de outubro.

item.title: Exlíder de banda criminal, condenado a entre 40 años y cadena perpetua por asesinato de Tupac Shakur
item.description: Un antiguo líder de una banda fue condenado el martes a una pena de entre 40 años y cadena perpetua por organizar el asesinato a tiros desde un vehículo en marcha de la estrella del hip-hop Tupac Shakur en Las Vegas en 1996.
item.dc:creator: Jack Queen, Steve Gorman
item.content:encoded: Un antiguo líder de una banda fue condenado el martes a una pena de entre 40 años y cadena perpetua por organizar el asesinato a tiros desde un vehículo en marcha de la estrella del hip-hop Tupac Shakur en Las Vegas en 1996. El fallo finalmente pone fin al proceso judicial de un caso que llevaba mucho tiempo sin resolverse y que marcó la edad de oro del rap. Duane "Keffe D" Davis, de 63 años, declarado culpable de asesinato en primer grado en agosto, recibió la pena durante una vista celebrada en un tribunal de Las Vegas. Hasta la detención de Davis en 2023, el asesinato de Shakur —que murió de un disparo en el asiento del copiloto de un todoterreno conducido por su ejecutivo discográfico, Marion "Suge" Knight— había sido durante casi tres décadas uno de los casos sin resolver más notorios de Estados Unidos. El asesinato, que acalló a uno de los artistas de rap más influyentes y con mayor éxito comercial, acentuó la imagen de violencia que impregnaba la cultura hip-hop de los años noventa, al tiempo que avivó la infame rivalidad entre el rap "gangsta" de la Costa Este y el de la Costa Oeste de esa época. A pesar de la condena de Davis, la cuestión de quién apretó el gatillo en el tiroteo mortal que acabó con la vida de la leyenda del rap de 25 años nunca se ha resuelto de forma concluyente. Davis fue juzgado y condenado por planear el asesinato para vengar la paliza que Shakur y miembros del séquito del rapero propinaron a su sobrino en el interior del casino MGM Grand, en el Strip de Las Vegas, el 7 de septiembre de 1996. Ha declarado que recurrirá su condena. El enfrentamiento en el casino se debió a la hostilidad entre dos bandas callejeras del área de Los Ángeles: los South Side Compton Crips, de los que Davis se autodenominaba líder, y los Mob Piru, asociados con Shakur, Knight y su discográfica, Death Row Records. Miembros de ambos grupos se encontraban en Las Vegas para asistir esa noche a un combate por el título mundial de boxeo de peso pesado entre Mike Tyson y Bruce Seldon. A las pocas horas de la pelea en el casino, Davis subió a su sobrino y a otros dos cómplices a un Cadillac blanco y se fue en busca de Shakur y Knight, decidido a ajustar cuentas, según el relato que Davis dio posteriormente a la policía en una investigación no relacionada con este caso y que la fiscalía citó durante su juicio por asesinato. Davis afirmó que pasó un arma a los dos hombres sentados detrás de él en el Cadillac, uno de los cuales abrió fuego a través de la ventanilla cuando alcanzaron y se pusieron a la altura del vehículo de Knight y Shakur en medio del tráfico. Shakur recibió cuatro impactos y falleció en el hospital seis días después. Knight, que sufrió una herida leve por un fragmento de bala que le rozó la cabeza, cumple actualmente una condena de 28 años de prisión por un delito de homicidio voluntario no relacionado con este caso. Las autoridades afirmaron que llevaban mucho tiempo creyendo que Davis estaba implicado en el asesinato de Shakur, pero carecían de pruebas suficientes para imputarle. Esto cambió cuando él mismo hizo pública su versión de los hechos en apariciones en la prensa y en unas memorias que, junto con las grabaciones de sus reuniones secretas con los investigadores, constituyeron la mayor parte de los argumentos de la acusación en el caso de asesinato. En su libro, "Compton Street Legend", el propio Davis escribió que se le consideraba sospechoso de los asesinatos tanto de Shakur como de Christopher Wallace, un rapero rival. Wallace, que actuaba bajo el nombre artístico de Notorious B.I.G. con el sello discográfico Bad Boy Entertainment, con sede en Nueva York, fue asesinado a tiros en Los Ángeles en marzo de 1997. Aunque el asesinato de Wallace sigue sin resolverse, desde hace tiempo se especula con que fue abatido a tiros en represalia por el asesinato de Shakur, ocurrido meses antes.

item.title: Anirban Lahiri urges people to 'chill out' amid 'dynamic' LIV 2.0 situation
item.description: Indian golfer Anirban Lahiri said the "situation is very dynamic" when asked Tuesday about LIV Golf, adding that the league's bankruptcy process will play out before he makes any final decisions about his playing future.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indian golfer Anirban Lahiri said the "situation is very dynamic" when asked Tuesday about LIV Golf, adding that the league's bankruptcy process will play out before he makes any final decisions about his playing future. With LIV Golf going through Chapter 11 bankruptcy, CEO Scott O'Neil has lined up BC Partners to help fund his vision for LIV 2.0. However, Spaniards Jon Rahm, Sergio Garcia and David Puig are among a group of players planning their exits from the league. Adrian Meronk reportedly has no intention of playing for LIV 2.0, and the Sports Business Journal reported Monday that Abraham Ancer intends to play on the DP World Tour in 2027. DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings said Monday that any player under contract with LIV 2.0 will not be eligible to compete on the European circuit in 2027. O'Neil is also facing a deadline in order to have enough players committed to LIV 2.0 in order to move forward. "A lot of things going on, it's hard for me to comment on it," Lahiri said ahead of this week's DP World Tour India Championship. "It's a matter of seeing how the processes work out. "I'm excited how I play this week. I think my focus and energies are going to be in the here and now, and next week I'm playing in Hong Kong. Then I do have the Philippines Open on my schedule, by which time I think we will know." Lahiri asked for continued patience as the situation with LIV 2.0 unfolds. "Just give it another month, month and a half, and everyone will know exactly what's happening one way or the other," Lahiri said. "LIV has been great for me and I've enjoyed it. Would I like for it to continue? Why not. But we don't have a crystal ball, so let's see where it goes." Lahiri said he has avoided reading the constant speculation about LIV's future over the past several months. He believes he has "a lot of gas left in the tank" and things he wants to achieve, but the decision about his playing future will hinge on what is best for his family. "Where I play is going to be based on the best interest of my family and myself. When that opportunity or option is put in front of me I'll exercise the best option," Lahiri said. "Outside of that, I don't pay attention to what's going on because there is no point. "There is nothing I can do to alter the larger scheme of things outside my own golf and the quality that I bring to a golf course, which is why I said that the best thing that everybody can do is chill out and wait for a month. Let things play out." --Field Level Media

item.title: Diplomático EEUU regresa a Washington tras rechazo Nicaragua de candidata a embajadora
item.description: El enviado interino de Estados Unidos a Nicaragua, Elias Baumann, ha regresado a Washington "para consultas cruciales" después de que funcionarios del país rechazaran a su candidata para ocupar el puesto de embajadora, Natasha Franceschi, informó el Departamento de Estado el martes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El enviado interino de Estados Unidos a Nicaragua, Elias Baumann, ha regresado a Washington "para consultas cruciales" después de que funcionarios del país rechazaran a su candidata para ocupar el puesto de embajadora, Natasha Franceschi, informó el Departamento de Estado el martes. La decisión de los copresidentes Daniel Ortega y su esposa Rosario Murillo "demuestra la hipocresía de su retórica de respeto mutuo y su deseo de participar en un espectáculo político a expensas del pueblo nicaragüense", añade el comunicado. La oficina de la Presidencia nicaragüense no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. Ortega ha acusado al Gobierno de Estados Unidos de intentar intervenir en los asuntos del país, incluso a través de organismos como el Parlamento Centroamericano y la Organización de los Estados Americanos (OEA). Nicaragua se encuentra sumida en una crisis política desde abril de 2018, y el Gobierno ha declarado que el país ya no celebrará elecciones. Estados Unidos dijo anteriormente que los servicios de seguridad de un país "no hemisférico" no identificado ha estado entrenando a la policía nicaragüense y compartiendo información de inteligencia. Nicaragua tiene acuerdos de cooperación en materia de seguridad con Rusia y China.

item.title: Zelenskiy seeks new talks with US envoys on ending Russia war
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Tuesday he had proposed new talks in the coming days with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner as Washington steps up efforts to bring Kyiv and Moscow back to negotiations.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Tuesday he had proposed new talks in the coming days with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner as Washington steps up efforts to bring Kyiv and Moscow back to negotiations. The proposal follows talks in the United States last week at which Witkoff and Kushner [USN:L1N45Y0OS TEXT:"told"] a Ukrainian delegation that a deal allowing Russian diesel exports was aimed at drawing Moscow back to negotiations. In his nightly video address, Zelenskiy also said Ukraine supported President Donald Trump’s proposed energy truce as long as Russia observed it. "Our team has sent the American side the relevant proposals regarding possible next meetings and conversations. In the coming days, we are ready to meet and I passed this proposal on to Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner through my team."

item.title: EEUU dice que diplomático destinado en Nicaragua regresa al país tras rechazo candidata a embajadora
item.description: El encargado de negocios de Estados Unidos en Nicaragua, Elias Baumann, ha regresado a Washington "para mantener consultas cruciales" después de que las autoridades del país rechazaran a la candidata para el cargo de embajadora, Natasha Franceschi, informó el martes el Departamento de
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El encargado de negocios de Estados Unidos en Nicaragua, Elias Baumann, ha regresado a Washington "para mantener consultas cruciales" después de que las autoridades del país rechazaran a la candidata para el cargo de embajadora, Natasha Franceschi, informó el martes el Departamento de Estado.

item.title: Cornell's sexual-assault investigation aims at transparency, but will findings become public?
item.description: In an attempt to quell the public outcry over Cornell University’s handling of sexual assault allegations, the Ivy League school’s board took a common step: call in the lawyers.
item.dc:creator: Sara Randazzo
item.content:encoded: In an attempt to quell the [USN:L1N45R111 TEXT:"public outcry"] over Cornell University’s handling of sexual assault allegations, the Ivy League school’s board took a common step: call in the lawyers. A team from King & Spalding, led by Justice Department veteran Sally Yates, [USN:L6N45S15B TEXT:"has been tasked"] with conducting an independent investigation into Cornell’s policies and procedures for addressing sexual harassment and assault on campus, including its response to the “Jane Doe” case that has [USN:L6N45O0CP TEXT:"drawn national attention"]. Cornell's board said it “intends to share the results and recommendations with the Cornell community," but education attorneys I spoke to said intentions can change and what's ultimately released could be limited to policy suggestions rather than a full dissection of what King & Spalding finds. Universities pledging transparency after a crisis face a competing interest of protecting themselves from further litigation. That tension, lawyers say, often leads universities to structure investigations to reduce the paper trail and reveal less than the public may expect. Cornell declined to comment beyond its statement announcing the law firm's hire. “The trend lately is: we don’t want anything in writing,” said Scott Schneider, a Texas-based education and employment lawyer who has done internal investigations for universities. He pointed to the recent example of the University of Michigan hiring Jenner & Block last year to conduct a culture review of its athletics department, but releasing only a summary of recommendations and actions rather than a full report. The university said it did so in part to maintain the confidentiality of the 300 witnesses interviewed and to preserve attorney-client privilege. OPENING THE DOOR An investigation a decade ago by Pepper Hamilton, now a part of Troutman Pepper Locke, into sexual assault allegations involving Baylor University football players shows the litigation risks universities face when publicly disclosing even limited results of outside probes. When Pepper Hamilton concluded its work, Baylor's board received an oral report from the lawyers and publicly released a 13-page findings of fact report along with 10 pages of recommendations on how to address the "fundamental failure" by the university to comply with Title IX, the federal law prohibiting sex discrimination in education and governing how schools respond to allegations of sexual harassment and sexual assault. A federal judge later agreed that women suing the university over Title IX violations were entitled to “all materials, communications and information” given to the firm, ruling in 2017 that Baylor waived its attorney-client privilege with the firm by putting out the findings of fact and recommendations. Three years later, another federal judge ordered even more documents related to the investigation to be produced. Universities hiring law firms to conduct investigations start with attorney-client privilege protections, but the release of any facts and conclusions can erode that protection. "Think of it as a door," Nancy Rapoport, a legal ethics professor at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, said in an email. "If no one opens the door, nothing can get out. If someone cracks open the door, lots of stuff can get out." In an earlier high-profile case, former FBI Director Louis Freeh’s 267-page report in 2012 finding Penn State officials covered up child sex abuse by assistant football coach Jerry Sandusky was [USN:620120712 TEXT:"widely viewed at the time"] as increasing the university’s liability. Attorneys called it a “road map” for civil claims, and judges later ordered the release of report materials. BROAD MANDATE In hiring Yates, Cornell chose a lawyer with experience handling investigations in both the government and private practice. Yates served as deputy US attorney general under former President Barack Obama and conducted a review for US Soccer into allegations of abusive behavior and sexual misconduct in women's soccer. Unlike some universities, US Soccer made public King & Spalding's full report, withholding only limited details to protect victims' confidentiality. Yates and a firm spokeswoman didn't respond to requests for comment. King & Spalding's mandate in the Cornell matter is broad, including an examination of how the university [USN:L1N45T0PE TEXT:"handles reports of sexual harassment or assault"], how students are supported, the role of campus police and other law-enforcement agencies and oversight of the Greek life system. Her team will also look at how the university responded to the 2024 incident of a Jane Doe alleging she was plied with drugs and alcohol, then sexually assaulted by members of a fraternity. Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff on Tuesday announced immediate changes to campus policies, including banning fraternity parties this academic year, noting that the university can't wait for Yates' work to be done before taking action. Doe [USN:L6N45Q051 TEXT:"filed a civil lawsuit last month"] against the university, seven fraternity members and other defendants. New York Governor Kathy Hochul then named the state's attorney general, Letitia James, to oversee a [USN:L1N45O00M TEXT:"reopened criminal investigation"]. The men have all [USN:L1N45U11G TEXT:"denied wrongdoing"], with some saying the sexual activity was consensual, while others disputed their participation. “It is imperative that Cornell be willing to examine itself with the same rigor we expect of others,” said Anne Meinig Smalling, chair of the board's special committee, which said the work will be done “as expeditiously and thoroughly as possible” without committing to a timeline. For Cornell, hiring Yates was the easy part. Deciding how much of her work to disclose could prove more difficult.

item.title: A.Latina mantiene resiliencia ante choques externos, dice Fitch Ratings, que proyecta menor crecimiento en 2026
item.description: América Latina ha demostrado capacidad para resistir nuevos desafíos externos en 2026, lo que ha respaldado la estabilidad y algunas acciones positivas en las calificaciones soberanas de la región, dijo el martes Fitch Ratings.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: América Latina ha demostrado capacidad para resistir nuevos desafíos externos en 2026, lo que ha respaldado la estabilidad y algunas acciones positivas en las calificaciones soberanas de la región, dijo el martes Fitch Ratings. En medio de ese escenario, Fitch proyecta que el crecimiento regional se desacelerará a 1,9% en 2026 desde el 2,2% del año pasado, afectado por enfriamientos en la mayoría de los países, incluido Brasil, aunque compensado parcialmente por una recuperación en México. Según la calificadora, las desaceleraciones obedecen más a factores domésticos y al fenómeno de El Niño que a las condiciones económicas globales, aunque estas también han influido. El choque en los precios del petróleo ha alimentado la inflación y reducido los ingresos reales en la región, con presiones adicionales esperadas por el fenómeno de El Niño. Asimismo, un endurecimiento de las condiciones financieras ante posibles nuevas alzas de tasas por parte de la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos podría actuar como un freno adicional. La agencia elevó la nota de cuatro soberanos en lo que va del año: tres de grado altamente especulativo -Argentina, Bolivia y Ecuador- y uno de grado de inversión, Aruba. Cuatro países mantienen perspectiva positiva (Aruba, Barbados, Costa Rica y Paraguay), mientras que la de República Dominicana fue revisada a estable. Ningún soberano de la región tiene perspectiva negativa. En el plano fiscal, las posiciones se han mantenido mayormente estables o en mejora durante 2026, impulsadas por ingresos extraordinarios provenientes de materias primas. No obstante, Fitch advirtió que el gasto público sigue bajo presión y que los recortes de inversión utilizados como alivio fiscal podrían ser difíciles de sostener. La agencia prevé deterioros fiscales significativos solo en Brasil y Colombia, donde las posiciones iniciales son débiles, y en Argentina y Paraguay, donde parten de niveles más sólidos.

item.title: サウジアラムコ本社付近で爆発音、リヤドでも警報発令
item.description: [１３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[１３日 ロイター] - サウジアラビアのダーランにある国有石油会社サウジアラムコの本社付近で１３日夜、大きな爆発音が聞こえた。関係筋６人がロイターに明らかにした。

ある関係筋によると、アラムコ本社が攻撃を受け、火災が発生した。ただ、直撃を受けたのか、落下した破片によるものかは不明という。４人の関係筋によると、建物に退避命令が出されていた。

サウジ主導の連合軍は、ダーランで迎撃・撃破したミサイルの破片が住宅地に落下したと発表したが、詳細は明らかにしなかった。

アラムコの従業員は１４日は在宅勤務とするよう指示された。アラムコから公式なコメントや事実関係の確認は得られていない。

サウジ当局はその後、首都リヤドで危険が生じる恐れがあるとして警報を発令。続いて同市内でも大きな爆発音が聞こえた。

item.title: Precios minoristas de Argentina +1,9% en septiembre: INDEC
item.description: El Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) de Argentina subió un 1,9% en septiembre, desde un 1,7% registrado el mes previo, dijo el martes el Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INDEC), un dato que se ubicó en línea a lo previsto por analistas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) de Argentina subió un 1,9% en septiembre, desde un 1,7% registrado el mes previo, dijo el martes el Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INDEC), un dato que se ubicó en línea a lo previsto por analistas. Un reciente sondeo de [USN:L1N45U0LZ TEXT:"Reuters"] proyectaba que el dato inflacionario del noveno mes del año se ubicaría en 1,9%. Así, el IPC en el año calendario arroja un incremento del 23,6% y alcanza al 33,4% de forma interanual. - Para más información ver

item.title: DOJ arrests two, seizes 187 devices in North Korean laptop farm crackdown in Texas
item.description: The US Department of Justice on Tuesday announced the arrests of two Americans accused of helping North Korean IT workers to steal identities and obtain fraudulent employment at US companies to earn money for the North Korean government.
item.dc:creator: A.J. Vicens
item.content:encoded: The US Department of Justice on Tuesday announced the arrests of two Americans accused of helping North Korean IT workers to steal identities and obtain fraudulent employment at US companies to earn money for the North Korean government. The agency announced the arrests of Michael James Bostelle, of Pennsylvania, and Juan Cecilio Pena Carrillo, of Texas, on charges of wire fraud, money laundering and identity theft as part of the alleged scheme, the DOJ said in a statement . As part of the crackdown, the DOJ announced that the FBI conducted searches and took other action between September 21 and September 25 at more than 40 residences in Texas thought to be operating as “laptop farms” for North Korean IT workers, the DOJ said. The FBI seized roughly 187 laptops and other devices used to carry out the scheme. The indictment also charged Sun Sheng Ming, Pei Li Guang, Weng Shou Cheng, Han Guo Bin, Wang Jian Jun, Sheng Zhang Kun, Zhang Wei Ping, Zhang Li Ping, Yu Yang and Jin Long, all based in China, for their roles in the operation, according to the statement. According to an indictment unsealed on Tuesday, the Chinese-based operators directed Pena and Tey Michael Nolte, along with at least four other Americans, in the scheme. Nolte was named in the indictment but not charged. Nolte and attorneys for Pena and Bostelle could not immediately be reached for comment. Emails sent to addresses that the DOJ alleged were used by the Chinese-based participants went unanswered. Nolte allegedly recruited, managed and trained Bostelle and other Americans, who allowed their names and personal information to be used to permit the North Korea-directed operation to function, in exchange for proceeds from the scheme, the DOJ said. The Americans’ actions included receiving and hosting laptops belonging to US victim companies at their homes, to make it appear as if the North Koreans were legitimate employees operating in the US. The “massive” fraud impacted more than 70 U. companies, compromised the identities of 25 Americans, caused false information to be sent to multiple US government agencies, and generated at least $3 million in revenue for the overseas IT workers, the DOJ said. The US government has for years warned of North Koreans surreptitiously gaining employment at US companies to raise money for the North Korean government, access company networks and steal data.

item.title: Top US diplomat to Nicaragua returns after US pick for ambassador rejected
item.description: The acting US envoy to Nicaragua, Elias Baumann, has returned to Washington "for critical consultations" after officials in the country rejected the US pick for ambassador, Natasha Franceschi, the State Department said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The acting US envoy to Nicaragua, Elias Baumann, has returned to Washington "for critical consultations" after officials in the country rejected the US pick for ambassador, Natasha Franceschi, the State Department said on Tuesday. The decision by co-Presidents Daniel Ortega and his wife Rosario Murillo "demonstrates the hypocrisy of their rhetoric of mutual respect and their desire to engage in political theater at the expense of the Nicaraguan people," the statement added. The Nicaraguan Presidency did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Ortega has accused the United States government of attempting to intervene in the country's affairs, including through bodies such as the Central American Parliament and the Organization of American States. Nicaragua has been in the grip of a political crisis since April 2018, and the government has said that the country will no longer hold elections. The United States has previously said that security services from an unnamed "non-hemispheric" nation are training Nicaraguan police and sharing intelligence. Nicaragua has security cooperation agreements with Russia and China.

item.title: Loud booms heard near Saudi Aramco headquarters in Dhahran, sources say
item.description: Loud booms were heard in the vicinity of Saudi Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran on Tuesday night, six sources told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Loud booms were heard in the vicinity of Saudi Aramco's headquarters in Dhahran on Tuesday night, six sources told Reuters. There was no official comment or confirmation from Aramco. One source said the Aramco headquarters was on fire. An evacuation order for the building had been issued, four of the sources said. A source with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters the Aramco headquarters had been struck, adding that it was unclear if the building had been hit directly or by falling debris. The Saudi-led coalition said fragments of a missile that it had intercepted and destroyed in Dhahran had fallen on a residential area without providing further details. Aramco employees were instructed to work from home on Wednesday, a direct source told Reuters. The Saudi civil defense later issued an alert of potential danger in the capital Riyadh and a loud boom was heard in that city afterwards.

item.title: 欧州市場サマリー（13日）
item.description:
＜ロンドン株式市場＞
まちまちで取引を終えた。英国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）や米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）などの発表を控える中...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（13日） 3:54 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞

まちまちで取引を終えた。英国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）や米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）などの発表を控える中、様子見姿勢が広がった。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は小幅に反落。一方、中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．０５％高。

ＦＴＳＥ３５０種貴金属株指数は１．３９％、鉱業株指数は１．７１％、それぞれ下落。銅大手アントファガスタは５．６％値下がりした。

ロンドン証券取引所グループ（ＬＳＥＧ）は４．７％安。金融データプロバイダーの買収に向けて協議していることを認めた。

石油大手のＢＰは３．７％高。２０２６年７─９月期の精製マージンが前年同期比で約３倍に拡大したとの推計を示し、買われた。

メルローズ・インダストリーズは３．５％高。広告大手ＷＰＰは４．２％高。

国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は、英国に対して財政赤字縮小を着実に進める必要があると指摘した。ただ、市場からは、今月２８日に発表を予定する英予算案について、増税措置などが限定的なものにとどまるとの見方が出ている。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞

３営業日ぶりに反落して取引を終えた。ハイテク関連株が売られた。ドイツのＤＡＸ指数とフランスのＣＡＣ４０指数はいずれも０．０７％下落した。

ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種テクノロジー株指数は１．６０％下落。中国の長鑫存儲技術（ＣＸＭＴ）の半導体設計を巡る報道を受け、競争激化に伴う業績への懸念が高まった。オランダの半導体製造装置メーカーＡＳＭインターナショナルは６．３％、フランスの半導体材料大手ソイテックは６．０％それぞれ下落した。

航空宇宙・防衛株指数は１．７３％安。

一部事業の売却で合意したフィンランドの通信機器大手ノキアは３．１％安だった。

ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州高級品株１０種指数は０．６１％下落した。直近四半期の売上高が市場予想を下回ったフランスの高級ブランドＬＶＭＨ（モエ・ヘネシー・ルイ・ヴィトン）は０．１％安。中国での購買意欲が低下したことが響いた。

一方、ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種化学株指数は２．０２％高だった。

直近四半期の販売が好調だったスイスの香料・香味メーカーのジボダンは９．４％上昇した。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞

長期債を中心に国債利回りが低下した。ハイテク株の下落を受け、安全資産である国債に資金が流入した。米国債の動きにも追随した。

ユーロ圏の指標となるドイツ１０年債利回りは、終盤に１ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）低下の３．４６％。一時は３．４２６％まで低下した。２年債利回りは３．１２５％とほぼ横ばいだった。

債券市場の混乱はここ数営業日でやや和らいだものの、相場はなお不安定だ。９月下旬から１０月上旬にかけての売りで、独１０年債利回りは２００９年以来の高水準となる３．６５％まで上昇していた。

１３日はハイテク株への警戒感が再燃し、典型的な安全資産への逃避として債券に資金が流入した。ナスダック１００先物は０．７％下落した。

ソシエテ・ジェネラルのアナリストはリポートで「米国債と独国債の買い戻しの動きは、リスク資産や半導体株の小幅な変調を受けたものだ。ただ、１４日の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）発表を控えたポジション調整が、買いの勢いをある程度抑えるだろう」とした。

幅広い市場で債券利回りは低下した。指標となる米１０年債利回りは３ｂｐ低下の５．２２％。フランス１０年債利回りは６ｂｐ低下の４．８４％、イタリア１０年債利回りは３ｂｐ低下の４．５５％となった。

仏独国債の利回り格差は、終盤時点で１３８ｂｐ。１０月上旬に付けた約１６０ｂｐという１４年ぶりの高水準を下回った。

イタリア１０年債利回りはフランス１０年債利回りを約３０ｂｐ下回った。ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、この差は少なくとも１９９０年代初め以降で最大の水準付近にある。

これは投資家の懸念が特にフランス国債に集中し、ユーロ圏の他国に混乱が広がるとの警戒感がひとまず和らいでいることを示している。

item.title: Report: Rams to release K Harrison Mevis, sign K Blake Grupe
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams will release Harrison Mevis and sign fellow kicker Blake Grupe off the New York Jets practice squad, NFL Network reported on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Los Angeles Rams will release Harrison Mevis and sign fellow kicker Blake Grupe off the New York Jets practice squad, NFL Network reported on Tuesday. The reported move comes after Rams head coach Sean McVay called out the team's kicking woes following a 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday. Mevis missed a field-goal attempt versus the Bills in regulation time and had another blocked in overtime. "The kicking game, especially with our PAT, field goal, not even close to good enough," McVay said. "It cost us the game tonight. ... I'm going to evaluate everything." Mevis, 24, made five of his last nine field-goal attempts, including just one of his last four over the past two games. He has made all 14 extra-point tries in five games. Grupe, 27, was claimed by the Jets off waivers from the Indianapolis Colts on Aug. 31. He has converted 81.9% of his field goals (86 of 105) and 98.0% of his PATs (96 of 98) in 50 games with the New Orleans Saints (2023-25) and Colts (2025). --Field Level Media

item.title: Berlin coalition talks suspended over antisemitism deal concerns
item.description: Germany's Greens and centre-left Social Democrats (SPD) suspended exploratory talks on forming Berlin's next state government with the far-left Left Party on Tuesday to assess whether antisemitism measures agreed to last week still stand.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Germany's Greens and centre-left Social Democrats (SPD) suspended exploratory talks on forming Berlin's next state government with the far-left Left Party on Tuesday to assess whether antisemitism measures [USN:L6N45U0H5 TEXT:"agreed to last week"] still stand. The proposed measures would allow lawmakers accused of antisemitism to be expelled if a panel came to a consensus on the matter. If they disagreed, experts would be called in. The decision comes after the Left admitted lawmaker Vanessa Emde, who has sparked controversy over her stance on Israel, as part of the state of Berlin's new parliamentary group. "We expect the Left to clarify the extent to which they intend to take the agreements we made seriously and implement them," the two parties said in a joint statement after the Left held a constituent meeting. The Left, a hard-left party represented in Berlin by lead candidate Elif Eralp, emerged from the September 20 state election as the largest force, with 25.7% of the votes. Left leader Luigi Pantisano said he was confident that talks could continue, adding that all elected representatives had signed a declaration committing themselves to the fight against antisemitism at their meeting on Tuesday. Tensions over antisemitism and the Israel-Gaza conflict have become a major fault line in German politics, with the SPD and Greens insisting on binding safeguards before entering exploratory coalition talks with the Left.

item.title: Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro reverses course, backs end to six-day workweek
item.description: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro on Tuesday said he would back a popular labor reform to reduce the country's workweek, reversing his position in a bid to avoid handing a political win to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, his leftist opponent in Brazil's presidential elections.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Cardoso
item.content:encoded: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro on Tuesday said he would back a popular labor reform to reduce the country's workweek, reversing his position in a bid to avoid handing a political win to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, his leftist opponent in Brazil's presidential elections. The measure, approved by [USN:L1N4230Q1 TEXT:"Brazil's lower house"] in May as a constitutional amendment, would lower working hours in Latin America's largest economy to 40 hours a week from 44, effectively ending a common practice in some sectors, like retail, of requiring employees to work six days a week. Bolsonaro, the son of former right-wing President Jair Bolsonaro, defied pollsters at the start of the month to lead President Lula in the first round of Brazil's election by securing 47% of votes cast. The two men will face each other in a runoff on October 25. Cutting the workweek would mark the biggest overhaul in Brazilian labor rights in decades and a nationwide poll conducted by Quaest in July found nearly 70% of Brazilians support the change. While the senator and his Liberal Party, PL, had long opposed cutting the workweek, arguing the move was designed to boost Lula's reelection prospects, Bolsonaro changed course on Tuesday, just a day before the Senate was expected to vote on the matter. "Most Brazilian workers want to see the end of the six-day workweek, so I'm going to vote in favor of ending it," Bolsonaro told journalists, adding that the government would need to offset impacts on business. Lawmakers aligned with Lula have pushed for a Senate vote before the runoff, hoping to secure approval while the president remains in office. "It seems to me that, following public pressure and street protests, PL decided to vote in favor of ending the six-day workweek," Lula said during an official event on Tuesday. The PL has yet to formally announce a change to its position. "Despite Flavio's lead, the race is still wide open. So it's a smart move by him in avoiding wearing down support on an issue that has broad popular appeal," Leandro Gabiati, director at political consultancy Dominium, said. While business groups say the measure could increase costs and hurt competitiveness, they will not be left too disappointed by Flavio's decision, Gabiati said. "The business community still has many ideological and practical reservations about this government," he said. "It will not feel betrayed by Flavio's change."

FRANKFURT, Oct 13 : The increased use of AI by euro zone companies could curb workers' ability to demand higher wages while heavy investment into the new technology may be materially tightening financing conditions, ECB chief economist Philip Lane said on Tuesday. With inflation now running at nearly twice the ECB's 2 per cent target on expensive energy, policymakers are searching for signs of second-round price effects, but have so far concluded there are none, especially in wage growth. While AI has not changed employment trends, hiring plans are muted and this limits workers' ability to demand compensation for high inflation, Lane said, offering a potential explanation for why wage growth is slowing, despite high inflation. "The potential for AI to replace some types of workers may also weaken the bargaining power of workers, moderating wage growth and reducing the labour share in total income," Lane said in a speech in Dublin.
