item.title: Russia detains Japanese journalist on suspicion of spying
item.description: Russia's FSB security agency said on Tuesday it had detained a Japanese journalist for alleged espionage, and Moscow's Foreign Ministry said it regretted that Tokyo was using correspondents to carry out spying.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia's FSB security agency said on Tuesday it had detained a Japanese journalist for alleged espionage, and Moscow's Foreign Ministry said it regretted that Tokyo was using correspondents to carry out spying. In a statement on its website, the FSB said the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper journalist was detained in the far eastern Sakhalin region on the day before he planned to leave Russia. It did not specify when this was. Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova in a statement identified the journalist as Imai Yuki, according to the Russian transliteration of his name, and said his detention cast a new pall on relations with Tokyo. Japan's embassy in Moscow did not answer phone calls outside of business hours. In a Russian state TV video report on the case, three masked men in black uniforms handcuffed a man lying on the ground as a voice off camera said he was suspected of spying. The video showed the man being accompanied by two FSB servicemen onto a plane, then in a cage in a Moscow court, which ordered him detained for nearly two months. The agency "thwarted the illegal activity" of the journalist, the FSB said. "As a result of intelligence operations, it was established that he gathered and stored information related to the country's defence capabilities in order to pass it on for national intelligence purposes to be used against the security of the Russian Federation," the statement said. The foreign ministry spokeswoman said, "Tokyo's attempts to use its correspondents in Russia with the status of foreign journalists to gather information for undermining our state's security are regrettable." Japan, she said, had adopted an anti-Russian position during Russia's military campaign in Ukraine and refused to consider Moscow's concerns about Tokyo's "remilitarisation". "We have to note that what has occurred will become an additional factor clouding the atmosphere of Russian-Japanese relations," Zakharova said. Russia regards Japan as an [USN:L8N3ZG0NU TEXT:""unfriendly" country"] because it has joined Western sanctions against Moscow over the war in Ukraine. Russia and Japan, which never signed a formal World War Two peace treaty, have a territorial dispute over the Kuril Islands, known in Japan as the Northern Territories. Russian President Vladimir Putin [USN:L8N44F0CG TEXT:"visited"] one of the disputed islands in August, causing an uproar in Japan. Tokyo has said it would continue implementing sanctions against Russia and supporting Ukraine. One of the most prominent cases of a foreign journalist arrested in Russia was the detention of Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich in 2023. He was found guilty of espionage by a Russian court, sentenced to 16 years and then freed in an East-West prisoner swap in August 2024.

seis importantes monedas, retrocedió un 0,37%, en consonancia con el descenso de los precios del petróleo y luego de que, en la víspera, la divisa estadounidense alcanzara un máximo de 18 meses. * El dólar amplió aún más sus pérdidas después de que el presidente de la Fed de Nueva York, John Williams, afirmara que sigue esperando una subida más de las tasas este año, pero que no ve necesidad de nuevas subidas en 2027. * En tanto, el Fondo Monetario Internacional recortó en la víspera sus previsiones de crecimiento para América Latina y el Caribe para 2026 y 2027, y dijo que la mayor parte de la región está recibiendo poco impulso del auge de la inteligencia artificial que ha ayudado a otras economías a absorber el choque energético de la guerra en Oriente Medio. * El peso mexicano cotizaba en 18,3771 por dólar, con una caída del 0,70%, reanudando una racha de pérdidas que había interrumpido en la víspera, mientras los inversionistas evaluaban señales sobre el futuro del diferencial de tasas entre México y Estados Unidos, con la mira puesta en la trayectoria monetaria de la Reserva Federal. * El principal índice accionario S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , que integran las 35 empresas más líquidas del mercado mexicano, subió un 0,33%, a 66.965 unidades, impulsado principalmente por firmas del sector financiero. * El real brasileño se depreció un 0,74%, a 5,0227 unidades por dólar, mientras que el índice Bovespa (.BVSP) de la bolsa B3 de Sao Paulo retrocedió un 1,08%, a 206.804,23 puntos. * En Argentina, el peso mayorista avanzó un 0,2% a 1.514 por dólar , el nivel más alto en casi un mes, en momentos en que el banco central (BCRA) busca sumar divisas a diario para respaldar sus reservas internacionales. * Con la idea de cubrir vencimientos de deuda interna a corto plazo, el Tesoro argentino realizará el miércoles su primera licitación mensual, una movida habitual debido a que tiene cerrada la posibilidad de financiamiento externo por los altos costos a pagar. * En tanto, el índice bursátil Merval (.MERV) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires escaló un 1,45%. * El peso chileno , sumó un ligero 0,04%, a 981,50/981,80 por dólar. En tanto, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) , cayó un 0,21%, a 11.020,01 unidades. * El peso colombiano ganó un 0,20% a 3.182,50 unidades por dólar y en la bolsa el índice accionario COLCAP (.COLCAP) subió 1,55% a 2.570,29 puntos. * La moneda peruana, el sol , finalizó con una apreciación de 0,12% a 3,4340/3,4370 unidades por dólar. Por su parte, la Bolsa de Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) retrocedió un 0,49% a 1.587 puntos.

item.title: Amnesty accuses F1 of offering Rwanda a 'sportswashing prize' with race deal
item.description: LONDON, Oct 13 : Human rights campaigners Amnesty International accused Formula One of hollow words and offering Rwanda a "sportswashing prize" with a 10-year African Grand Prix deal announced on Tuesday.The landmark deal envisages a race sometime in the early 2030s, at a circuit that has yet to be built near

Amnesty accuses F1 of offering Rwanda a 'sportswashing prize' with race deal

FAST

LONDON, Oct 13 : Human rights campaigners Amnesty International accused Formula One of hollow words and offering Rwanda a "sportswashing prize" with a 10-year African Grand Prix deal announced on Tuesday. The landmark deal envisages a race sometime in the early 2030s, at a circuit that has yet to be built near a new international airport to the south of Kigali. It will be the first race in Africa since 1993. "A 10-year Grand Prix 'presented by Visit Rwanda' is a sportswashing prize for the Rwandan authorities," said Felix Jakens, Amnesty UK's head of campaigns in a written response. "Arsenal, Aston Villa, the cycling world championships and now Formula One - Rwanda is buying into the world's biggest sports to polish its image and deflect from its appalling human rights record.

"Formula One says sport can be 'a positive force for good'. That rings hollow if F1 shrugs off who it is partnering with. Rwanda's authorities are prolific in arbitrary detention, torture and the repression of free speech – these are abuses at home." The Rwandan government did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The allegation of "sportswashing" is levelled at countries perceived to be using sport to improve a tarnished image abroad. Several other Formula One hosts, mainly in the Middle East, have been accused of it. Premier League side Aston Villa's sponsorship agreement with Visit Rwanda drew similar criticism from human rights campaigners last July. The African nation's tourism board also has sponsorship agreements with Atletico Madrid and Paris St Germain, as well as US sports teams including the Los Angeles Clippers and Los Angeles Rams. It had branding on Arsenal's shirt sleeves for eight seasons. Rwanda's President Paul Kagame has won praise from Western and regional leaders for helping to end the 1994 genocide in Rwanda and rebuilding the country into an attractive destination for investment and aid. He also stands accused of a crackdown on critics at home, and supporting the M23 rebel group in neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo, who rights groups say are guilty of killings, rapes and other rights abuses. Kagame told a press conference in Kigali that the deal would set Rwanda on a journey "that will change how Africa is perceived in the world of sport". "We are looking at Rwanda in the context of a continent," he added. A Formula One spokesperson said the sport had "the opportunity to inspire and bring the passion of F1 to 100 million people across Africa and sport can be a positive force for good."  Jakens urged Formula One to push for change "rather than lend its brand to a PR exercise."

Source: Reuters

item.title: ロシア、ウクライナのエネルギー施設攻撃せず トランプ氏「停戦」発表後初
item.description:
Olena Harmash Daniel Flynn
[キーウ １３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Olena Harmash　Daniel Flynn

[キーウ　１３日　ロイター] - ロシアは１３日、トランプ米大統領が週末の間に「エネルギー停戦」を発表して以来初めて、ウクライナのエネルギー関連施設への攻撃を実施しなかった。ただ、ウクライナ各地の輸送・物流インフラを標的にした攻撃は続けた。

トランプ米大統領は１１日、ロシアとウクライナが双方のエネルギー関連施設への攻撃停止で「合意した」と自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）に投稿。即時発効するとしたが、詳細は明らかにしなかった。ロシア大統領報道官はこの件について協議は続けられていると述べるにとどめ、詳細な説明は避けているが、 ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は１３日、トランプ米大統領が「エネルギー停戦」を発表したことを受け、ロシアの製油所などのエネルギーインフラへの攻撃を２日間停止したと明らかにしていた。

ロシア国防省は１３日に公表した夜間攻撃に関する日次報告でウクライナのエネルギー施設に対する攻撃について言及していない。ただ、今回の攻撃でロシアがエネルギーインフラを意図的に攻撃対象から外したかどうかは現時点では明らかになっていない。

＜輸送・物流インフラへの攻撃続く＞

ウクライナ空軍は１３日、夜間のロシア軍による攻撃で国内１７カ所で被害が確認されたと明らかにした。防空部隊がロシア軍のドローン（無人機）１０８機のうち８８機を撃墜したとしている。

西部リビウで市内の大部分に熱供給を行う施設から１キロ余り離れた場所にミサイル１発が着弾したほか、南部ミコライウ州では貨物ターミナルが被害を受け、南東部ドニプロペトロフスク州では輸送インフラが損傷した。ウクライナ第２の都市ハリコフでは集合住宅への攻撃により４人が死亡し、少なくとも１１人が負傷した。西部フメリニツキー州では病院が被害を受けた。

ウクライナ空軍は、ロシアが１２日夜に首都キーウに向けて弾道ミサイル６発を発射した際、事前の監視・警戒情報がなかったと表明。空軍は声明で「原因を調査している」としている。

ロイターなどは、米当局者がウクライナに対しロシアの製油所への攻撃を停止しなければ、情報共有や武器売却を打ち切る可能性があると警告したと報道。ただ、ウクライナのシビハ外相はこの日、ウクライナは米国から引き続き情報提供を受けていると表明。ワルシャワ安全保障フォーラムで「ウクライナと米国は協力を継続している」と述べた。

item.title: 米中古住宅販売、9月は予想外の1.5％増 住宅ローン金利上昇で先行き懸念も
item.description: [ワシントン １３日 ロイター] - 全米リアルター協会（ＮＡＲ）が１３日発表した９月の米中古住宅販売戸数（季節調整済...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米中古住宅販売、9月は予想外の1.5％増　住宅ローン金利上昇で先行き懸念も 10/13 23:43 配信

米カリフォルニア州エンシニタスの住宅に掲げられた「売家」の看板。１月撮影。REUTERS/Mike Blake

[ワシントン　１３日　ロイター] - 全米リアルター協会（ＮＡＲ）が１３日発表した９月の米中古住宅販売戸数（季節調整済み）は年率換算で前月比１．５％増の３９９万戸だった。在庫の増加により買い手の選択肢が広がったことから予想（３９５万戸）に反して増加した。ただ、住宅ローン金利の上昇を背景に伸びは依然として鈍い。

９月は前年同月比では２．２％減少した。

地域別では、南部と西部で増加した一方、北東部では減少し、中西部では横ばいだった。

ＮＡＲのチーフエコノミスト、ローレンス・ユン氏は「季節調整済みベースでは前月比で小幅な増加が見られたものの、８月と９月は今年に入って住宅販売が最も低調な２カ月となった」と指摘。「ここ数週間の住宅ローン金利の一段の上昇により、住宅購入の資格を満たせる買い手は減少している」と述べた。

中古住宅の在庫は１．９％増の１６０万戸と、２０１９年１１月以来の高水準となった。前年同月比では４．６％増加した。

９月の販売ペースに基づく在庫の消化期間は４．８カ月と、前月から横ばいだったが、前年同月（４．５カ月）の水準を上回った。

中古住宅価格の中央値は前年同月比１．３％上昇の４１万７５００ドルと、同月としては過去最高となった。初めて住宅を購入する人の割合は全体の３１％と、前月および前年同月の３０％から上昇した。

住宅が市場に出ていた期間の中央値は３３日。前月の３１日からは延びたものの、前年同月からは横ばいとなった。

差し押さえ物件を含む不良債権売却は取引全体の２％と、変わらずだった。

現金のみによる販売の割合は２７％と前月から横ばい。前年同月は３０％だった。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か コラム：トランプ米大統領、任期中の利下げは望み薄　市場は高金利長期化を想定 焦点：トランプ政権の影で歩み寄るカナダとＥＵ、準加盟提示でも見える限界 最終更新: 10/13(火) 23:43 ロイター

item.title: Goolsbee says AI-induced inflation is 'jumping out of its lane,' Semafor reports
item.description: Oct 13 : Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said on Tuesday that inflation is starting to feel like "aggregate overheating" fueled by spillovers from the artificial intelligence investment boom rather than largely being a byproduct of supply shocks that will pass on its own."This is sta
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Business

Goolsbee says AI-induced inflation is 'jumping out of its lane,' Semafor reports

FILE PHOTO: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee is interviewed on the sidelines of the Kansas City Fed's annual economic symposium, in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, U.S. August 27, 2026. REUTERS/Ann Saphir/File Photo

13 Oct 2026 10:39PM

Get bite-sized news via a new cards interface. Give it a try.

Click here to return to FAST Tap here to return to FAST

FAST

Oct 13 : Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said on Tuesday that inflation is starting to feel like "aggregate overheating" fueled by spillovers from the artificial intelligence investment boom rather than largely being a byproduct of supply shocks that will pass on its own. "This is starting to feel like aggregate overheating, that the AI data center cost increases are jumping out of its lane, that prices are going up in spaces that are not just components in data centers and the directly adjacent industries to data centers," Goolsbee said in a Semafor interview. "If you start to see more of this spreading into general services, that investment goods are just getting GDP (gross domestic product) growth up faster than potential and generating this kind of spillover inflation, that’s problematic because unlike supply shocks where we tend to assume they’re going to go away on their own in a relatively short period of time, nobody thinks that of overheating demand." "It takes a long time for overheated demand to get going, and once it’s going, it’s hard to get rid of that," Goolsbee said. "So that’s why the conventional wisdom among economists has been if you see overheating demand, you act decisively and you act quickly to prevent that from rolling into inflation expectations, rolling into people taking for granted that it’s never going to go away." Asked whether the Fed should continue raising interest rates, Goolsbee, who does not have a vote on rate policy this year, said: "So if inflation remains persistent, then I think it’s clear what the Fed has to do. If we can get some evidence that this tariff inflation is going away, that the oil shock inflation is going away, it’s not too much progress that we need to show, but we need to start showing some progress if we’re going to get back on the kind of rate cutting path that we were on." The Fed cut rates three times in 2025 but last month raised rates for the first time in three years in the face of stubborn inflation, bumping its short-term policy rate up by a quarter percentage point to a range of 3.75 per cent-4.00 per cent. Rate futures markets expect it will forego another increase at the coming October 27-28 meeting but will lift rates by another quarter point in December.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Can Senegal's debt restructuring revamp the Common Framework?
item.description: When Senegal disclosed billions of dollars of previously unreported borrowing two years ago, investors assumed it was headed for a familiar debt crisis playbook: an IMF programme, lengthy creditor negotiations and years of uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: Marc Jones, Anait Miridzhanian, Colleen Goko
item.content:encoded: When Senegal disclosed billions of dollars of previously unreported borrowing two years ago, investors assumed it was headed for a familiar debt crisis playbook: an IMF programme, lengthy creditor negotiations and years of uncertainty. Instead, Dakar is hoping for something more ambitious. Its bid to restructure its debt within [USN:L8N45S13U TEXT:"months"] while securing a new $2.2 billion [USN:L6N44T0WZ TEXT:"IMF bailout"] is shaping up as a test of whether sovereign debt workouts can be made faster and less disruptive. The country wants to use what it calls an "[USN:L6N44T0WZ TEXT:"enhanced"]" version of the Common Framework, the G20 mechanism launched in 2020 to coordinate debt restructurings, but has faced [USN:L8N36G41M TEXT:"criticism"] over lengthy negotiations and disputes over burden sharing. Senegal has already held initial [USN:L8N45M0UW TEXT:"information-sharing"] sessions and parallel consultations with stakeholders in an effort to prevent the years-long delays suffered by the likes of [USN:L5N3G52D0 TEXT:"Zambia"] and [USN:D7N37G017 TEXT:"Ghana"]. The effort ties into [USN:SPN45Z0XN TEXT:"broader discussions"] at this week's IMF and World Bank meetings on speeding up restructurings. [USN:L1N4560ZW TEXT:"World Bank"] President Ajay Banga has already backed Senegal's approach, while IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva called the efforts [USN:L6N45800F TEXT:""encouraging""], although it remains unclear whether all creditors will support the plan. Four African countries have gone through the Common Framework. "Senegal is the perfect opportunity to get this process right because so many other countries are on the brink but don't want to go for the Common Framework because of its issues," said Kevin Gallagher, a professor of global development policy at Boston University. "It needs to be quicker," he added, saying that for many countries the scale of debt relief also needed to be much larger and losses more "fairly distributed" between creditors. NEED FOR SPEED Central to Senegal's plan to streamline the process are four parallel creditor committees. A presentation to investors last week seen by Reuters showed that, alongside the standard groups representing bilateral lenders and bondholders, Dakar has proposed separate committees for commercial banks and regional development institutions, areas where complications have emerged for other countries. A government source said the Paris Club of creditor nations had indicated a deal could be reached within six to nine months, possibly sooner. The Paris Club did not respond to a request for comment. And speed matters. Dakar has been trying to restore investor confidence since President Bassirou Diomaye Faye's administration revealed in 2024 that the previous government [USN:L8N44U172 TEXT:"substantially understated"] the debt burden. Subsequent audits pushed debt estimates to around 130% of GDP, including state-owned enterprises and government-guaranteed borrowing, triggering downgrades, a bond selloff and suspension of its IMF programme. A new $2.2 billion IMF deal is now being negotiated, but the Fund will need assurances that Senegal's problems are being comprehensively addressed before [USN:L8N45N19R TEXT:"approving"] it. "I don't have a timeline yet for exactly when we will be able to bring the programme to our Executive Board," IMF spokesperson Julie Kozack told reporters this month. Economists say Senegal enters the process with important advantages absent in other recent restructurings. Moody's analyst Aurelien Mali points to offshore oil and gas production, economic growth and access to regional financing markets and development bank funding. The use of West Africa's CFA franc – pegged to the euro – has helped keep inflation under control, rare for a crisis-hit nation, he added. As a result, the challenge is seen less as preventing economic collapse than restoring fiscal credibility. END THE SQUABBLES Another sign that Senegal intends to take a different approach was the IMF's involvement in the government's [USN:L8N45S13U TEXT:"investor call"] last week, something not seen in previous Common Framework cases. Zambia's Finance Minister Situmbeko Musokotwane said he hoped lessons from his country's nearly four-year restructuring ordeal had been learned. If faster negotiations can also secure broad creditor participation, it would strengthen the argument that the Common Framework can become a more market-friendly instrument. "Countries that came behind us obviously have benefited from the improvements," Musokotwane told Reuters, referring to the Common Framework process. "So I'm happy for them, happy for those who are coming behind." Restructuring experts nevertheless see potential obstacles. Dakar wants to exclude billions of dollars worth of CFA franc-denominated debt given the headache it could cause its neighbours, but that means more losses elsewhere. There's also nearly $1.3 billion it borrowed using complex derivatives known as [USN:L6N40E1D4 TEXT:"Total Return Swaps"] to untangle. The IMF has also stressed that there is only one Common Framework, pushing back against references to an "enhanced" version. Veteran debt lawyer Lee Buchheit warns too that disputes among bilateral creditors can drag on for years. Yvette Babb, an emerging market fund manager at William Blair, said it all pointed to a delicate balancing act. The government must convince the IMF and creditors that it is addressing its debt scandal, while assuring markets that a restructuring will not lead to prolonged financial isolation. "It really is going to be a big test," Babb said.

item.title: 米ゴールドマン、第3四半期利益が予想上回る 株式部門収入が72％増
item.description:
Saeed Azhar Pritam Biswas
[１３日 ロイター] - 米金融大手ゴールドマン・サックスが１３日...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米ゴールドマン、第3四半期利益が予想上回る　株式部門収入が72％増 10/13 23:18 配信

米ゴールドマン・サックスのロゴ。2025年12月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Saeed Azhar　Pritam Biswas

[１３日　ロイター] - 米金融大手ゴールドマン・サックスが１３日発表した第３・四半期（７─９月期）決算は利益が市場予想を上回った。ディールメーキングが堅調に推移したほか、中東紛争を背景にした市場のボラティリティー（変動率）が株式部門の収入を押し上げた。

ソロモン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は声明で「世界情勢が現在、複雑かつ不確実であるにもかかわらず、当社は引き続き顧客に貢献し続けられる非常に良いポジションにある」と述べた。

第３・四半期の総利益は５２億９０００万ドル、１株当たり利益は１７．０１ドル。前年同期はそれぞれ４１億ドル、１２．２５ドルだった。ＬＳＥＧがまとめたアナリスト予想は１３．０２ドルだった。

株式部門の収入は前年同期比７２％増の６４億４０００万ドル。一方、債券・通貨・商品（ＦＩＣＣ）部門の収入は１％減の３４億７０００万ドルとなった。

アーガス・リサーチのアナリスト、ステファン・ビガー氏は「ＦＩＣＣは最近のカンファレンスで示唆されていた通りやや軟調だったが、投資銀行部門は市場予想を上回った。これは取引案件のパイプラインが依然として堅調であることを示しており、今後数四半期にわたって同部門の収入は高水準で推移する見通しだ」と述べた。

投資銀行部門の手数料収入は前年比２１％増の３２億２０００万ドル。債券・株式の引受業務の拡大と、アドバイザリー収入の１８％増により、市場全体の減速に逆行する結果となった。アドバイザリー部門の収入は同行として過去最高となった。

同行は、インテルによる２３０億ドル規模の株式発行の共同主幹事を務めたほか、韓国ＳＫハイニックスの２６５億ドル規模の米国での株式発行ではグローバルコーディネーターを担当した。

また、ニューヨーク・ヤンキースによるプライベートキャピタル大手アポロ・スポーツ・キャピタル関連会社との２６億ドルの資金調達案件や、半導体大手エヌビディアによる台湾の半導体メーカー、メディアテックへの３５億ドルの投資案件についてもアドバイザリー業務を提供した。

資産運用・ウェルスマネジメント事業の収入は１４％増加し、再び堅調な四半期となった。これにより、総純収入は２３％増の１８６億８０００万ドルと、過去２番目の高水準となった。

ゴールドマンの株価は午前の取引で１．６％上昇した。同社の株価は２０２６年に入り約１．７％上昇にとどまっており、同業のモルガン・スタンレーやＳ＆Ｐ総合５００種をアンダーパフォームしている。

item.title: UK police arrest three suspected of involvement in insider dealing ring
item.description: Three people have been arrested in Britain on suspicion of being involved in a criminal insider dealing and money laundering plot, the Financial Conduct Authority said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Three people have been arrested in Britain on suspicion of being involved in a criminal insider dealing and money laundering plot, the Financial Conduct Authority said on Tuesday. More than 100 staff and officers searched five residential premises in London and the northern English city of Manchester in a joint operation with the National Crime Agency, seizing more than 30 mobile phones, laptops and tablets, the FCA said. "Insider dealing is a serious threat to the integrity of our markets," the FCA's joint enforcement head, Steve Smart, said in a statement. "Working with partners, we will continue to use all the powers at our disposal to crack down on serious and organised crime groups engaged in market abuse." The FCA, which said it could not comment further at this stage, secured four insider dealing convictions last financial year, with two resulting in record, [USN:L1N3T10JD TEXT:"combined prison sentences"] of 11 years. The regulator has stepped up enforcement action on suspected insider dealing, with recent cases involving an [USN:FWN3YG1OG TEXT:"oil rig consultant"], [USN:L1N3LF0N0 TEXT:"traders"] and a financial adviser .

FAST

Oct 13 : Hyundai Motor Group said on Tuesday it would invest $15.5 billion in India through 2032, deepening its bet on the world's third-largest car market as a key driver of future growth.  The South Korean automaker's seven-year plan includes about $700 million of investment in its Indian research and development centre, expansion of production capacity and a dedicated investment entity. India, the world's third-largest car market, is attracting billions of dollars in investment from global automakers seeking to tap rising demand and expand local manufacturing capacity, underscoring its position as a major automotive production hub.  Hyundai said last year it would invest $5 billion to expand its manufacturing and research operations in India.

Japan's Suzuki Motor , the majority owner of India's largest carmaker by volume, Maruti Suzuki, also laid out plans in 2025 to invest about $8 billion in the country. Carmakers such as Toyota and Honda have committed to expanding their manufacturing ambitions in India as well.  Hyundai Motor, which employs more than 24,000 people in India, said the investment would create additional jobs across manufacturing, research, engineering and supply chains, but did not disclose a number.  The firm said the investment plan, covering 2026 to 2032, would expand manufacturing capacity at Hyundai Motor India and Kia India to support significant volume growth. The investment also includes a vehicle testing track, as part of efforts to develop next-generation automotive technologies. The investment announcement followed a meeting between Hyundai Motor Group Executive Chair Euisun Chung and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Tuesday. The group currently has an annual production capacity of more than 1.4 million vehicles in India, comprising 824,000 units at Hyundai's Chennai facilities, 170,000 units at its Pune plant and 431,000 units at Kia's Anantapur facility.

item.title: Trump fires ambassador to Greece Guilfoyle after reports of misconduct
item.description: The White House said on Tuesday it had asked US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign after a series of news reports raised concerns she sold access to Trump administration officials in exchange for money, gifts and favors.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bogage , Edward Mcallister, Simon Lewis
item.content:encoded: The White House said on Tuesday it had asked US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign after a series of news reports raised concerns she sold access to Trump administration officials in exchange for money, gifts and favors. US President Donald Trump had said on Monday that he was considering firing Guilfoyle, who was once engaged to his son Donald Trump Jr. On Tuesday, he told reporters: "She was doing a good job, but we didn't like what we were reading." US lawmakers had raised the alarm after a series of stories in the Wall Street Journal beginning last month that detailed Guilfoyle's conduct, including claims she threatened to use US influence to undermine the Greek government. New White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia confirmed Guilfoyle had been asked to resign, telling a briefing: "She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well." In a post on X, Guilfoyle repeated denials of wrongdoing and said her gratitude and respect for Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio remained "unwavering." "While my time as Ambassador may be coming to an end, my commitment to President Trump, the America First movement, and the country I love will never end," she wrote. "These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity." One of the reports published by the Journal described Guilfoyle's close relationship with a lobbyist for a Greek energy company and her promotion of that firm, while another cited audio recordings of Guilfoyle bragging about her ties to wealthy Greek businessmen as she sought an invitation to a Davos dinner honoring another of Trump's sons, Eric. US businessman Eric Deters also told the newspaper that Guilfoyle, a former San Francisco prosecutor, had offered access to Trump administration officials for money, at one point asking him to pay her $100,000 credit card bill. Britain's Daily Mail reported last week that the State Department's internal watchdog was looking into complaints of inappropriate behavior from staff at the Athens embassy. The Greek government has not commented on the allegations involving her tenure as ambassador. Neither the State Department nor Washington's embassy in Athens responded to requests for comment. DEALS AND DIPLOMATIC WAVES Greece has been an important NATO ally of the United States, offering key military facilities to safeguard security in the Eastern Mediterranean, and it leads an EU maritime mission to protect commercial shipping in the Red Sea. During a visit to Athens last week, Rubio said Greece and the US were launching new counterterrorism information sharing between their law enforcement agencies. Guilfoyle's tenure in Athens was high profile from the start as she appeared on the cover of Vogue Greece and attended late-night parties with Greek celebrities. She aggressively touted American interests, including signing deals for the import of US liquefied natural gas and [USN:L6N3WI0FW TEXT:"drilling deals involving companies including Exxon Mobil"]. But she also created diplomatic waves. In her first interview with local media after arriving last November, she said China should sell its 67% stake in the port of Piraeus, which has become a cornerstone of Beijing's Belt and Road Initiative. China’s ambassador to Greece, Fang Qiu, responded by accusing the US of having "an outdated and a harmful mentality" and "a hegemonic mindset." Dimitris Mantzos, foreign affairs spokesperson for Greece’s opposition PASOK party, said Guilfoyle’s firing raised serious issues and unanswered questions. Would Greek officials demand an explanation, he said, or "content themselves with watching the country serve as a 'theater'" for outside interests.

item.title: Rams' Alaric Jackson gets 2-game ban for punching Bills' Bradley Chubb
item.description: Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson was suspended two games by the NFL for punching Buffalo Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb after Los Angeles lost Monday night in overtime.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson was suspended two games by the NFL for punching Buffalo Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb after Los Angeles lost Monday night in overtime. Chubb was spotted talking to players on both teams near midfield after the Bills' 37-34 overtime victory over the Rams when he appeared to say something to Jackson. The 6-foot-7, 338-pound Jackson walked toward Chubb -- 6-4 and 268 pounds -- and punched him in the jaw. "It's just emotions, you know what I mean? Emotional game, it was a close game," said Chubb, who was pulled away from the confrontation. "They always catch the second guy, so I let him swing, and then my teammates held me back, and I just chilled." Jackson, 28, was pulled away by Rams tight end Colby Parkinson after the punch. He will lose paychecks while missing the Rams' next two games -- against the Arizona Cardinals this week and at the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7. He is eligible to rejoin the Rams following the Raiders game Oct. 25. Chubb, 30, said he was fine after the incident. "I'm just ready for next week," he said. "You see me, I'm smiling, I'm with my team. I'll be ready for next week." Chubb and the Bills (4-1) will visit the Raiders on Sunday. --Field Level Media

item.title: US Supreme Court to hear asylum fight involving Nigerian cook
item.description: The US Supreme Court agreed on Tuesday to hear a bid by President Donald Trump's administration to deny asylum to a man who was forced to prepare meals for an apparent separatist group in Nigeria, in a case that could expand what officials may deem terrorist activity under American immigration law.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Chung
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court agreed on Tuesday to hear a bid by President Donald Trump 's administration to deny asylum to a man who was forced to prepare meals for an apparent separatist group in Nigeria, in a case that could expand what officials may deem terrorist activity under American immigration law. The justices took up the Justice Department's appeal of a lower court's ruling in favor of Nigerian citizen Izuchukwu Ozurumba, who was denied US asylum due to his work cooking for a group known as the Unknown Gunmen that US officials considered to be a terrorist organization. The lower court ruled that cooking did not qualify as "material support" for terrorism under the immigration statute. The Supreme Court is expected to hear arguments and rule in the case by the end of June. The administration, in appealing the case to the Supreme Court, said that if the lower court's ruling were allowed to stand, it would "substantially increase the burden on the government in excluding aliens with links to terrorism." The case centers on whether Ozurumba's work for the group fell under provisions of US immigration law that bar the entry of non-US citizens who have "engaged in a terrorist activity," including actions that provide "material support" for such activity or "to a terrorist organization." "At stake in this case is whether the government can use an overly broad reading of the law to shut the door on people seeking asylum," said Aimee Mayer-Salins, an attorney with the Amica Center for Immigrant Rights, which is helping to represent Ozurumba. The lower court "correctly recognized that asylum should not be denied to immigrants who provided no meaningful support to a terrorist group," Mayer-Salins added. Following a job tip in 2022, Ozurumba took a van to a remote camp outside of Lagos, according to court papers. After he was hired, he eventually learned the camp was run by the Unknown Gunmen, a group likely associated with Nigerian separatists, according to court papers. Ozurumba soon "observed that the young men's movements from the camp coincided with news reports of murder and arson," his lawyers said in a court filing. Ozurumba sought to leave but was forced to stay without pay, they added. After six months he escaped while on an outing for supplies, eventually making his way back to Lagos, they said. Ozurumba then faced beatings and threats of death, prompting him to flee to Venezuela, where the threats continued, his lawyers said. Ozurumba then traveled to the southern US border and entered the country illegally in July 2023. Ozurumba eventually applied for asylum and other protections from deportation. 'BASIC HUMAN NEEDS' During Democratic former President Joe Biden's administration, an immigration judge deemed the Unknown Gunmen a terrorist organization and found that Ozurumba's cooking for the group rendered him inadmissible, and denied him any protections from deportation. The judge concluded that the cooking helped the group accomplish its goals by satisfying their "basic human needs," and that it was irrelevant that he had worked under duress. Ozurumba was deported back to Nigeria last year while his case was on appeal. The Richmond, Virginia-based 4th US Circuit Court of Appeals sided with Ozurumba in September 2025, ruling that he was a captive laborer and his cooking did not constitute material support. Ozurumba's work "provided nothing that the organization could use or readily divert to plan or carry out its terrorist activities," the 4th Circuit ruled, but declined to order the government to return him to the US while the case proceeds. "Providing meals to a terrorist organization's members is no less a material form of support than providing gasoline for its vehicles," the Justice Department told the Supreme Court in its appeal.

By Tala Ramadan and Yomna Ehab Oct 13 (Reuters) – A Saudi-led coalition urged civilians on Tuesday to evacuate the Yemen Oil Company’s Sabah central station in the capital Sanaa ahead of a planned military operation.

A statement from the coalition’s joint forces command identified the site on a map and said civilians should leave the area for their own safety.

A military spokesperson for Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis, Yahya Saree, warned that any strikes on Sanaa would be met with a “harsh and painful” response in the Saudi capital Riyadh.

The Houthis also warned employees and civilians near Saudi Aramco oil facilities to evacuate and stay away, saying the facilities were legitimate targets for their forces.

Fighting has escalated between the Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis, who have been attacking Saudi airports and oil facilities since last week in a spillover from the wider regional conflagration between the US and Iran.

Saudi Arabia has in recent weeks launched strikes against the Houthis and is backing a Yemeni government counteroffensive after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.

The conflict has disrupted air travel in Saudi Arabia, with Riyadh airport remaining closed after a deadly missile strike on Saturday claimed by the Houthis.

item.title: Missile hits headquarters of Saudi Aramco, source says, as Houthi conflict escalates
item.description: A ballistic missile hit the headquarters complex of Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company, the world's largest and the backbone of the kingdom's economy, a company source told Reuters, amid an escalating war between Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari, Menna Alaaeldin
item.content:encoded: A ballistic missile hit the headquarters complex of Saudi Arabia's state-owned oil company, the world's largest and the backbone of the kingdom's economy, a company source told Reuters, amid an escalating war between Yemen's [USN:L1N45Q02Z TEXT:"Iran-allied Houthis"] and a Saudi-led coalition. An office tower in the Saudi Aramco complex in the eastern city of Dhahran was struck on Tuesday night and the top three floors were damaged, the source said. The source and two other people with knowledge of the matter said the building was on fire. The complex hosts a major operations centre for Aramco, which oversees a vast network of onshore and offshore oil rigs, pipelines, refineries and export terminals. Earlier, six sources told Reuters they heard loud booms near the complex. There was no official comment from Saudi Aramco. The Saudi-led coalition said fragments of a missile that it had intercepted and destroyed in Dhahran had fallen on a residential area, without providing further details. Authorities also reported that drones and missiles were intercepted and destroyed in the capital, Riyadh, and the country's southern region. The Houthis had earlier threatened a "harsh and painful" response to Saudi-led strikes on the Yemeni capital Sanaa, with spokesperson Yahya Saree saying targets could include the Saudi Aramco headquarters in Dhahran and an oil refinery in Riyadh. The group has warned oil workers in Saudi Arabia to stay away from sites that could be targets. The Houthis have for a week been firing ballistic missiles and drones at key Saudi sites in retaliation for the kingdom's backing of government forces against the Houthis in Yemen's reignited civil war. Riyadh’s international airport has received four strikes, including one on Saturday that killed 13 people. The Houthis earlier on Tuesday said Saudi Arabia was attacking Sanaa, and the Saudi-led coalition warned civilians to stay away from an oil depot on the city's outskirts. Houthi-run Al-Masirah television reported that the Saudi-led coalition had targeted the Yemen Petroleum Company's Sabah central station, a fuel depot on the outskirts of Sanaa. The coalition said in a statement on Tuesday evening that it attacked the station and other sites in an operation aimed at "neutralizing the capabilities of Houthis" to threaten Saudi Arabia, Yemen and international waterways. The Saudi cabinet, chaired by de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, issued a statement on Tuesday before the strike on Saudi Aramco saying the Houthis would face consequences for their repeated attacks on the kingdom. Saturday's ballistic missile strike on Riyadh airport was the deadliest in Saudi Arabia in a decade, with further attacks grounding flights across the country even as it hosts a major energy conference. REIGNITED YEMEN WAR Saudi Arabia resumed its military campaign in Yemen in support of the internationally recognised government in a bid to reverse the Houthis' sudden gains last month, when they swept down the Red Sea coast to the critical Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The strait, the southern gateway to the Red Sea, has become a more vital route for Saudi and other global energy supplies since the start of the Iran war in February, when Tehran closed the Strait of Hormuz leading from the Gulf to the Indian Ocean. While a government offensive that began a week ago pushed the Houthis from the area closest to the strait, the group remains embedded nearby and has made gains around the city of Taiz this month. Saudi Arabia has been seeking wider support from allies for its campaign against the Houthis and to help it ward off their missile and drone attacks. Washington, Saudi Arabia's strongest ally and longtime security guarantor, has so far rebuffed Saudi efforts to bring it directly into the war against the Houthis. The Yemen conflict has resumed as a spillover from the wider US-Iran war that began with the US-Israeli attack on the Islamic Republic on February 28. Iran, Saudi Arabia's longtime regional archrival, has offered to mediate between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, its foreign minister Abbas Araqchi said on Sunday in statements reiterated by the ministry on Monday.

item.title: Le pape Léon XIV a subi l'ablation d'un lobe pulmonaire, un cancer détecté-Vatican
item.description: Le pape Léon XIV a subi mardi une intervention chirurgicale lors de laquelle le lobe inférieur de son poumon droit a été retiré, alors qu'un adénocarcinome - une forme courant de cancer pulmonaire - a été détecté, a fait savoir le Vatican dans un bulletin médical.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le pape Léon XIV a subi mardi une intervention chirurgicale lors de laquelle le lobe inférieur de son poumon droit a été retiré, alors qu'un adénocarcinome - une forme courant de cancer pulmonaire - a été détecté, a fait savoir le Vatican dans un bulletin médical. Des analyses moléculaires réalisées durant l'opération ont confirmé ce que les médecins suspectaient au regard des résultats des examens préparatoires à cette intervention, a ajouté le Vatican. Un peu plus tôt dans la soirée, le Vatican a déclaré que l'opération s'était bien passée. Le souverain pontife, âgé de 71 ans, a annoncé dimanche qu'un nodule pulmonaire, détecté à un stade précoce, avait été localisé lors d'un récent bilan de santé et qu'il était "bien circonscrit". Léon devrait rester en convalescence environ une semaine. Tous ses engagements publics ont été annulés jusqu'au 20 octobre.

FAST

AMSTERDAM, Oct 13 : Dutch supermarket company Ahold Delhaize has no indication that client data has been stolen in the cybersecurity incident that forced it to shut down several systems in recent days, it said in a statement on Tuesday. The Dutch retailer, which operates the Netherlands' largest supermarket chain Albert Heijn and has major operations in other European countries as well as the United States, said on Monday that it was dealing with a "security issue" on its network and had taken several systems offline as a precaution. The incident coincided with a cyberattack in France which saw refrigerators and freezers at hundreds of stores heating up to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) overnight, sparking fires and spoiling food. The Dutch National Cyber Security Centre has said that there is no reason to believe that there is a link between the incident in the Netherlands and similar incidents in other countries.

Source: Reuters

LONDON, Oct 13 : Facebook and Instagram owner Meta challenged Britain's media regulator on Tuesday over how it calculates fees and potential fines under the Online Safety Act, arguing that the watchdog's methods are disproportionate. The 2023 law allows Ofcom to impose fines of up to 10 per cent of qualifying worldwide revenue, or £18 million ($23.9 million), whichever is greater, and to recover the costs of running its regime through fees calculated by reference to revenue. Meta's challenge comes a week after Ofcom opened an investigation into whether the company properly assessed the risks posed by its Instagram Instants feature before launching it in May. The case brought by Meta opened in London's High Court on Tuesday and centres on Ofcom's use of worldwide rather than UK revenue to determine fees and maximum potential fines.

Meta argued that Ofcom had exceeded its statutory powers by defining qualifying worldwide revenue as broadly as possible, with the objective of imposing the highest possible penalties. That was Ofcom's "overriding concern", Meta said in its legal submission. Meta is also challenging Ofcom's method of calculating fines where two or more providers owned by the same organisation are found jointly liable for breaches. Ofcom argues that its approach is proportionate and that it has struck a "careful balance" in defining qualifying revenue. Its court submission said that qualifying worldwide revenue was used only to calculate the maximum potential penalty and that any actual fine must be proportionate to the failure. Meta is also fighting Ofcom on other fronts. It joined TikTok and X in a separate legal hearing last week over the amount of information the regulator is demanding. Meta said it was committed to cooperating constructively with Ofcom. "However, we and others in the tech industry believe its decisions on the methodology to calculate fees and potential fines are disproportionate," a Meta spokesperson said. "We believe fees and penalties should be based on the services being regulated in the countries they're being regulated in. This would still allow Ofcom to impose the largest fines in UK corporate history." Ofcom said it had been tasked with regulating an industry that had been unregulated and unaccountable for more than 20 years. An Ofcom spokesperson said Meta's case was one of a number of legal challenges it faced.  "On all these fronts, we will robustly defend our reasoning and decisions," the spokesperson said. BENGALURU, Oct 13 : An influential Hindu nationalist group close to India's ruling party urged the government on Tuesday to block Elon Musk's Starlink from launching satellite internet services in the country, citing national security concerns. Starlink's four-year wait to launch in India has come under renewed scrutiny after Musk last week accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government and billionaire Mukesh Ambani of stalling its entry to favour Ambani's Reliance Jio. India's communications ministry said last week that security assessments were under way for Starlink and rival satellite ventures backed by Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel. It described suggestions the approval process was unfair or discriminatory as "baseless and misconceived". The call for Starlink's ban came from Swadeshi Jagran Manch (SJM), the economic wing of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), the Hindu nationalist organisation that is the ideological parent of Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party.

SJM also linked its demand to trade tensions with the US. If Washington imposes high tariffs on Indian imports "in the name of national security, then India is certainly within its rights to block Starlink based on its genuine national security concerns," national co-convenor Ashwani Mahajan said in a statement. Starlink's technology could make it difficult for authorities to restrict internet services during security emergencies and ensure Indian internet traffic passes through domestic infrastructure, Mahajan added. SJM has influenced Indian policy in recent years, notably pushing for rules to protect small traders from US-owned e-commerce firms Amazon and Walmart's Flipkart. SpaceX, Starlink's parent company, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. MARKET WITH MORE THAN A BILLION INTERNET USERS Starlink is seeking to launch in a country with more than a billion internet subscribers. Alongside Starlink, satellite ventures backed by Reliance Jio and Bharti are awaiting final clearances to begin services. Musk has repeatedly taunted Ambani on X, questioning why Starlink still lacked a licence despite what he said were years of compliance with Indian requirements. "Is Ambani the real boss of India?" he posted last week, as he accused the rival billionaire of stalling Starlink's entry.

Oct 13 : Bumble is set to go private in a $1.3 billion deal with Ithaca Holdings after struggling for years to revive growth, as a prolonged decline in users and shifting Gen Z dating habits batter the online dating industry. Shares of the company soared 56 per cent to $5.95 in early trading on Tuesday, after surging 50 per cent on Monday following media reports on the Ithaca deal. Bumble and larger rival Match, which owns Tinder and Hinge, have been battling declining user engagement, as younger users increasingly grow tired of swiping endlessly on apps and seek more organic ways to build connections. Match has so far outperformed Bumble with its portfolio of apps that cater to niche demographics, as well as international growth at Hinge, which draws users with its detailed, relationship-oriented profile formats.

"With Hinge having gained and continuing to gain share of more intentioned daters, Bumble's niche has eroded. The management, brand, and strategy changes have also not helped," said Chandler Willison, TMT Research Analyst at M Science. Bumble said Ithaca co-founders Ravi Gupta and John Hegeman will become Bumble's co-CEOs after the takeover. The firm has offered $6.05 per share for Bumble, representing a 122.4 per cent premium to the stock's closing price on June 24, a day before Reuters exclusively reported the company was exploring a sale. AI TOOLS YET TO SPUR RECOVERY Founded in 2014 by Whitney Wolfe Herd, Bumble pioneered the "women-first" approach to online dating that has been a defining feature for the company. But it rolled back the feature this year in a bid to improve its user retention rates. Under Herd, who returned as CEO in March 2025 after stepping down in 2023, the company has tried everything from raising prices and extending reply windows to adding AI tools that help users craft messages and exploring offline events to keep users hooked. It has also been testing a new AI matchmaking assistant in response to traditional swiping fatigue. But that has failed to aid its recovery. Total paying users fell 16.4 per cent to 3.2 million in the second quarter, while quarterly revenue has been declining for nearly two years. Bumble's market value has shrunk to about $582 million as of Monday's close, a far cry from its $14 billion valuation when it went public in 2021. Blackstone, which owns about 14 per cent of Bumble, according to LSEG data, and Herd have provided required shareholder approval for the deal.

Source: Reuters

item.title: 韓国・仁川の商業施設で8人刺される、男拘束 1人重体
item.description: [ソウル １３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ソウル １３日 ロイター] - 韓国警察は１３日、仁川市のショッピングモールで８人を刺した疑いで男を拘束したと発表した。聯合ニュースによると、被害者の１人は重体となっている。

警察によると、動機や事件の詳しい状況を捜査中。聯合ニュースが伝えた目撃者の話によると、男は両手に刃物をくくり付けていたとみられ、モール内の複数の階を移動しながら人々を襲った。その後、居合わせた人々に取り押さえられ、警察に引き渡された。

被害者は女性６人と男性２人。２０代の女性１人が命に関わる重傷を負い、近くの病院で手術を受けたという。

聯合ニュースによると、容疑者は５９歳で、殺人未遂で懲役４年の刑で服役していた。

法務省は声明で、男は２０１９年の出所後、監視用の電子足輪を装着しており、精神面の問題やアルコール依存症の治療を受けていたと明らかにした。電子監視制度は、殺人などで有罪判決を受けた人を対象とする犯罪防止策。

同省は、全地球測位システム（ＧＰＳ）によるリアルタイムの位置情報で追跡するこの制度について、徹底的に検証すると表明した。

仁川はソウルの西に位置する首都圏の一部で国際空港がある。

item.title: Dólar cae desde máximo de 18 meses, mercado aguarda datos de inflación
item.description: El dólar retrocedió el martes desde su máximo de 18 meses, a medida que los precios del petróleo bajaban y los inversionistas reevaluaban el repunte impulsado por la inteligencia artificial que ha respaldado la demanda de activos estadounidenses este año, a la espera de nuevas pistas sobre la trayectoria de las tasas de la Fed.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Rebaudo, Laura Matthews
item.content:encoded: El dólar retrocedió el martes desde su máximo de 18 meses, a medida que los precios del petróleo bajaban y los inversionistas reevaluaban el repunte impulsado por la inteligencia artificial que ha respaldado la demanda de activos estadounidenses este año, a la espera de nuevas pistas sobre la trayectoria de las tasas de la Fed. * "El dólar está retrocediendo a medida que crece el escepticismo sobre la solidez y la sostenibilidad de las valoraciones bursátiles relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial, lo que amenaza con frenar las entradas de capital en los mercados financieros estadounidenses", afirmó Karl Schamotta, estratega jefe de mercados de Corpay en Toronto. * El dólar amplió aún más sus pérdidas después de que el presidente de la Fed de Nueva York, John Williams, afirmara que sigue esperando una subida más de las tasas este año, pero que no ve necesidad de nuevas subidas en 2027. * Esto provocó que el índice del dólar estadounidense —que mide la fortaleza del dólar frente a una cesta de seis divisas— cayera un 0,37 %, hasta situarse en 102,18, tras alcanzar el lunes los 102,61, su nivel más alto desde abril de 2025. * Los mercados esperan que el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, evite una escalada en Oriente Medio, ya que un conflicto más amplio podría perjudicar su imagen de cara a las elecciones de mitad de legislatura del próximo mes. * Trump afirmó la semana pasada que EE. UU. no atacará a Irán antes de las elecciones, y el domingo mencionó un alto el fuego en materia energética entre Rusia y Ucrania. * Los precios del petróleo cayeron un 0,75 % hasta situarse en 105,87 dólares por barril el martes, mientras los operadores sopesaban la posibilidad de un aumento del suministro de gasóleo ruso. Rusia afirmó que puede restablecer las exportaciones de gasóleo por encima de los niveles que Trump esbozó en un acuerdo con Moscú. * Más allá del sector energético, los analistas señalaron que el reciente repunte del dólar también se ve amenazado por las crecientes dudas sobre el potencial de inversión impulsado por la inteligencia artificial. * Los inversionistas esperan ahora la publicación, el miércoles, del índice de precios al consumo de Estados Unidos correspondiente a septiembre, que debería aportar más pistas sobre un posible endurecimiento de la política monetaria de la Fed. * Los inversionistas abandonaron sus apuestas por una subida de tasas de la Fed a finales de este mes después de que dos responsables de política monetaria abogaran por recabar más datos antes de decidir si es necesario un mayor endurecimiento, mientras que el gobernador de la Fed, Christopher Waller, afirmó que las expectativas de inflación seguían "bien ancladas". * El yen se apreció un 0,18 %, hasta situarse en 158,33 frente al dólar, después de que los datos del Banco de Japón mostraran que los precios al por mayor subieron un 6,8 % en el año hasta septiembre, por debajo de la previsión media del mercado del 7,6 %, pero lo suficiente como para justificar los temores del mercado ante una subida de las tasas de interés.

item.title: Investigators hunt French supermarket fridge hackers, no claim of responsibility
item.description: French investigators on Tuesday were hunting the hackers who seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets in a cyberattack that underlined the vulnerabilities of connected systems, with no group publicly claiming responsibility.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Satter, Gabriel Stargardter
item.content:encoded: French investigators on Tuesday were hunting the hackers who [USN:L8N45Y11U TEXT:"seized control of cooling units"] at hundreds of supermarkets in a cyberattack that underlined the [USN:L6N45Z0J7 TEXT:"vulnerabilities of connected systems"], with no group publicly claiming responsibility. The investigation comes as Dutch supermarket company Ahold Delhaize (AD.AS) grapples with a separate cybersecurity incident that disrupted online services, although Dutch authorities said they saw no connection between the two events. The absence of a claim of responsibility by hacktivists or a ransom demand by cybercriminals has puzzled French investigators, according to a source with knowledge of the probe. Typically, such groups tend to quickly seek to monetise their hacks or claim credit for them for political ends. The cyberattack, which manually overrode the temperatures at fridges in supermarket groups including Carrefour (CARR.PA) , Monoprix, Intermarche and Cooperative U, appears to have been easy to pull off, three cyber experts told Reuters. Staff at some Paris supermarkets threw boxes full of perished meat and frozen goods into giant trash containers on Tuesday. At least 350 supermarkets — a small fraction of the total number in France - were caught up in the strike. FIRM BLAMES OUTDATED SOFTWARE France's cybersecurity agency has said the breach affected fridges that relied on software by Danish firm Danfoss, as well as Copeland and Dixell software. Danfoss said on Monday that many of the affected units had "reached end of life and no longer receive software or security updates" or were "running outdated firmware." It said it had "advised customers to keep supported systems updated with the latest firmware and to migrate legacy systems to current-generation solutions". The company declined further comment on Tuesday. Copeland, which owns Dixell, acknowledged the "vulnerability." "We are currently working with impacted customers to mitigate the risk," the company said, adding that it would strengthen cybersecurity. In Danfoss' case, the serious vulnerabilities present in older versions of its firmware have been known for months. On August 9, cybersecurity firm Claroty detailed weaknesses - since patched - in the Danfoss AK-SM 800A controller that could have allowed intruders to bypass authentication and run code on compromised devices. 'BASIC CYBER HYGIENE' Although the precise mechanism by which attackers compromised the refrigerators has not been publicly disclosed, cybersecurity experts said all signs pointed to a basic stunt enabled both by the failure to adopt Danfoss' updates and by exposing device interfaces to the internet. "This is about basic cyber hygiene," said Ken Munro, a partner at the British cybersecurity firm Pen Test Partners. "Get it wrong and you get a smelly mess of defrosted food." He said the well-known vulnerabilities meant the attackers were essentially pushing at an open door, something that meant the hack could easily be "kids messing around". "If this was a nation state, why affect only a subset of French fridges? There are plenty of other nations with fridges on the internet," he said. "No ransom or demand suggests a lack of appreciation of the potential commercial losses that the fridge owners may experience." PROBLEM STILL EXISTS Plenty of fridges remain reachable via the internet. Using the internet scanning service Shodan, Reuters found at least 4,500 Danfoss interfaces still viewable on Tuesday. Reuters could not independently establish how many of them were running vulnerable software, but French internet scanning company Onyphe said only a small minority of the devices appeared to be running the latest version of the software. Outdated and vulnerable versions were "still widely represented among publicly accessible interfaces", Onyphe said. DUTCH DISRUPTION Separately, Dutch retailer Ahold Delhaize [USN:S8N42D059 TEXT:"said on Tuesday"] that it had begun "starting a controlled re-launch of certain systems" following a cybersecurity issue that began on Sunday evening. The Dutch cybersecurity watchdog NCSC said it did not believe the incident was linked to the French supermarket hack. Ahold operates the Albert Heijn chain in the Netherlands and several major US chains including Stop & Shop and Giant Food. Websites for stores in both countries remained offline late Tuesday afternoon, with online ordering and delivery services unavailable.

item.title: Cirugía del papa León fue exitosa y se desarrolló según lo previsto, reporta el Vaticano
item.description: La intervención quirúrgica a la que se sometió el martes el papa León para extirpar un pequeño nódulo en uno de sus pulmones se desarrolló con éxito y según lo previsto, dijo el Vaticano, unas siete horas después de que el pontífice fuera ingresado en el hospital por el primer problema de salud grave de sus 17 meses de pontificado.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee, Matteo Negri
item.content:encoded: La intervención quirúrgica a la que se sometió el martes el papa León para extirpar un pequeño nódulo en uno de sus pulmones se desarrolló con éxito y según lo previsto, dijo el Vaticano, unas siete horas después de que el pontífice fuera ingresado en el hospital por el primer problema de salud grave de sus 17 meses de pontificado. León, de 71 años, fue atendido en el hospital Gemelli de Roma para la extirpación del pequeño nódulo, que, según declaró el pontífice el domingo, se había detectado en una fase temprana durante un reciente chequeo médico. "La intervención se completó con éxito, dentro del plazo previsto y según lo planeado", indicó un breve comunicado del Vaticano emitido a última hora del martes, que no ofrecía más detalles. El Vaticano había informado anteriormente que la intervención fue dirigida por el jefe de cirugía torácica del Gemelli, el profesor Stefano Margaritora. León salió del Vaticano antes de la intervención, poco antes de las 1100 GMT en Roma, y se le vio saludando con la mano desde la parte trasera de un todoterreno negro mientras su comitiva recorría unos 9 km al norte del Vaticano hasta llegar al Gemelli. Al llegar al hospital, León estrechó la mano a varios funcionarios, pasó ante una multitud de simpatizantes que le esperaba —algunos de los cuales gritaban "Auguri" (mis mejores deseos)— y entró por la entrada principal. Según los expertos médicos, la intervención quirúrgica del martes debería ayudar a determinar si el tumor es maligno o qué tratamiento adicional es necesario. El Vaticano no especificó en su comunicado de la tarde qué pruebas se le habían realizado al nódulo. El Vaticano ha indicado que se espera que el papa se recupere en el hospital durante aproximadamente una semana. Se han cancelado todos sus actos públicos hasta el 20 de octubre. UN PAPA RELATIVAMENTE JOVEN León, elegido por los cardenales de todo el mundo en mayo de 2025, es relativamente joven para ser un líder de la Iglesia. Le gustan los deportes, incluido el tenis, y no se sabe que fume ni que haya tenido problemas de salud recientemente. Un nódulo pulmonar es una pequeña lesión localizada que puede ser benigna. La Sociedad Torácica Americana afirma que menos del 5% de los nódulos pulmonares resultan ser cancerosos, aunque el riesgo aumenta con la edad, el tamaño y otros factores como el tabaquismo. El doctor Federico Venuto, jefe de cirugía torácica del Hospital Policlínico Umberto I de Roma, explicó que las intervenciones para extirpar nódulos pulmonares suelen ser mínimamente invasivas y, en ocasiones, pueden implicar el uso de un tubo con cámara delgada denominado toracoscopio. "La tasa de complicaciones es extremadamente baja", declaró a Reuters. VIAJE A SUDAMÉRICA El difunto papa Francisco, predecesor de León, fue hospitalizado en varias ocasiones a medida que su salud se debilitaba en sus últimos años. Falleció a los 88 años en abril de 2025. León, que habló con voz firme y clara en su único acto público del lunes, mantiene una agenda muy apretada. Tiene previsto realizar una gira de 11 días por Uruguay, Argentina y Perú del 6 al 17 de noviembre. Someterse a la intervención quirúrgica sin demora le ofrece la mejor oportunidad de mantener su viaje por Sudamérica según lo previsto. La suite del Gemelli donde suelen alojarse los papas durante el tratamiento no está disponible actualmente porque se está renovando. El papa es la máxima autoridad terrenal para los 1.400 millones de católicos del mundo y no cuenta con un suplente que le sustituya cuando está enfermo. Cuando un pontífice se encuentra incapacitado, la actividad de la vasta burocracia del Vaticano continúa con normalidad, aplazándose aquellas decisiones que requieran la aprobación papal. FIEBRE TIFOIDEA León, nacido en Chicago en 1955 como Robert Prevost, ejerció durante décadas como misionero y obispo en Perú antes de convertirse en papa. En 1985, cuando era un joven sacerdote, contrajo la fiebre tifoidea en Chulucanas (Perú) y fue hospitalizado. Relató la experiencia en la única entrevista importante que concedió como papa, en un libro publicado por Penguin Perú. León dijo que el dolor era tan intenso que le pidió a Dios que le dejara morir antes que seguir sufriendo. Interpretó su supervivencia como una señal de Dios de que "te necesitamos aquí (en la Tierra)", afirmó. "Nunca miré atrás", afirmó León.

item.title: ウェルズ・ファーゴ、第3四半期利益は予想超え 純金利収入は届かず
item.description: [１３日 ロイター] - 米大手銀行ウェルズ・ファーゴが１３日発表した第３・四半期決算は、１株当たり利益が市場予想を上回...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ウェルズ・ファーゴ、第3四半期利益は予想超え　純金利収入は届かず 10/13 20:33 配信

ウェルズ・ファーゴのクレジットカード REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

[１３日 ロイター] - 米大手銀行ウェルズ・ファーゴが１３日発表した第３・四半期決算は、１株当たり利益が市場予想を上回ったものの、純金利収入と総収入は予想に届かなかった。

１株当たり利益は１．８７ドル。ＬＳＥＧがまとめたアナリストの平均予想の１．８５ドルを上回った。

純金利収入は５％増の１２５億２０００万ドルとなったが、市場予想の１２６億３０００万ドルには届かなかった。変動金利資産の適用金利低下や預金コストの上昇、無利息預金の減少が純金利収入に影響した。

２０２５年に１兆９５００億ドルの資産上限規制が解除されたことを受け、同行はバランスシートを拡大し、大手競合にシェアを奪われていた事業での巻き返しを図っている。

ただ融資残高の急拡大に伴い、将来の貸し倒れに備えた引当金も増加。同行は延滞動向に悪化は見られないとしている。

貸倒引当金繰入額は１０億３０００万ドルと、前年同期の６億８１００万ドルから増加した。

総収入は２１８億７０００万ドルとなり、市場予想の２２３億１０００万ドルを下回った。

ウェルズは良好な消費動向を取り込み、クレジットカードと自動車ローンを軸に個人向け融資残高を拡大してきた。

チャーリー・シャーフ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は声明で「経済の先行きは不透明で消費者心理もまちまちだが、当行のデータを見る限り個人・法人顧客の状況はいずれも良好だ」と述べた。

マイク・サントマッシモ最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）は決算発表後の電話会見で「借り手にも預金者にも、これまで見られた基調に変化が生じていると思わせるような行動の変化は見られない」と述べた。

＜投資銀行業務はまちまち＞

同行は投資銀行・市場部門に多額の資金を投じており、幹部級のバンカーを採用するとともに、顧客向け融資やトレーディング、その他の資本市場業務への支出を増やしている。

この戦略により、同行は投資銀行業務のランキングで順位を上げ、ネクステラ・エナジーによる同業ドミニオン・エナジーの６７０億ドルでの買収など、２０２６年の大型案件の一部で助言業務を獲得した。第３・四半期には、トーマ・ブラボーによるアクセララントの４０億ドル超での非公開化で助言を担った。

第３・四半期の投資銀行業務収入は前年同期比１０％増の６億１１００万ドルだった。ただ借り入れコストの上昇が重しとなり、前四半期比では３％減少した。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める アングル：ドル高支える年金基金のヘッジ巻き戻し、市場環境変化で懸念後退 アングル：今年はバリュー投資が活発化か、ＡＩバブル懸念で着目点変化 アングル：米株のテック依存、「ＩＴバブル期」上回る　市場を不安定に アングル：米国株、人気は株主還元よりＡＩ技術革新投資の企業 最終更新: 10/13(火) 22:08 ロイター

item.description: THE HAGUE: Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay urged the United States on Tuesday (Oct 13) to return to its traditional role of defender of human rights and liberator for the rest of the world amid a
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Nobel peace laureate Navi Pillay urges US to defend human rights

THE HAGUE: Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay urged the United States on Tuesday (Oct 13) to return to its traditional role of defender of human rights and liberator for the rest of the world amid a US campaign to undermine the International Criminal Court.  "My message is: 'You have to get back to playing your serious role as a leader, playing a liberatory role for the rest of the world'," Pillay, 85, told Reuters in The Hague, where she is currently a judge at the United Nations' highest legal body, the International Court of Justice.   Hours after Pillay was announced as the winner of the Peace Prize on Friday, the United States announced sweeping sanctions aimed at her former employer, the International Criminal Court.  She said the timing of the sanctions, an unprecedented attack on an institution founded by international treaty, right after her Nobel Prize win could not be coincidental.

"I think it's very unfortunate. However, the plans of targeting international criminal justice through the ICC were brewing all the time," Pillay said. "That's why the first thing I did when I returned from Nuremberg to The Hague is to go to the staff of the ICC to show solidarity for their work in promoting international criminal justice and to protect those who've already been sanctioned." US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday called the ICC a "rogue court" that would never be allowed to prosecute Americans. The new sanctions were suspended for six months, and included some other exemptions for transactions for telecoms, software, payment of pensions and transactions related to detainees. The US has long been hostile to the court, and especially the ICC statute that says it has jurisdiction not only over nationals of member states but also over others alleged to have committed atrocity crimes on the territory of member states.

item.title: 機関投資家、米10年債6％近くなら株から資金移動＝ＢｏＦＡ調査
item.description: ［ロンドン １３日 ロイター］ - 投資家が株式から債券に資金を移すほど債券の魅力が高まるには、米１０年債利回りが６％...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
機関投資家、米10年債6％近くなら株から資金移動＝ＢｏＦＡ調査 10/13 20:27 配信

ドル紙幣 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

［ロンドン　１３日　ロイター］ - 投資家が株式から債券に資金を移すほど債券の魅力が高まるには、米１０年債利回りが６％近くまで上昇する必要があることが、米バンク・オブ・アメリカ（ＢｏＦＡ）が１３日公表した１０月の世界ファンドマネジャー調査で分かった。金利が大きく上昇する中でも、株式市場の底堅さを保っていることが背景にある。

調査は１０月２─８日に実施した。投資家の楽観度は６月以来の低さとなったが、米中間選挙と第３・四半期の決算シーズンに向けて、マクロ経済と市場については依然として強気な見方を維持した。

１０月調査の主な結果は以下の通り。

・世界経済の成長見通しについて悲観的な見方に転じた。今後１２カ月で景気が悪化すると予想する割合は差し引きで４％。インフレ期待は２０２５年１月以来の低水準に下がった。

・債券利回りに対する悲観的な見方は２５年５月以来の低水準。長期金利の上昇を予想する割合は差し引き１％と、９月の１５％から低下。

・市場にとって最大のテールリスクは債券利回りの無秩序な上昇。次いで人工知能（ＡＩ）バブル。

・最も活発だった取引は引き続き「世界の半導体株の買い持ち」で、次いで「米国債の売り持ち」。

・ＡＩハイパースケーラー（大規模クラウド事業者）の設備投資は、システミックな信用イベントの最も可能性の高い発生源と引き続き見なされている。

・ハイテク株のオーバーウエートは２０年８月以来の高水準。一般消費財株のアンダーウエートは０８年７月以来の高水準。

・銀行株への配分は、２３年３月以来の大幅な減少。

・配分が増えたのは債券、日本株、英国株、公益株。

・配分が減ったのは銀行株、米国株、一般消費財株。

・投資家の７６％が、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は１０月に政策金利を据え置くと予想。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：中国政府、株市場てこ入れ作戦に公的年金基金も動員 アングル：世界の債券市場揺らす日本マネー、長期金利3％で還流の兆し コラム：ＡＩ投資巡る強気・弱気論争が先鋭化、株価は乱高下 焦点：ラッセル指数銘柄入れ替えで26日は米株取引急増か、スペースＸなど注目 アングル：中国株「熱狂でない上昇」に海外勢回帰、強気相場は半ばとの見方も 最終更新: 10/13(火) 20:27 ロイター

item.title: グレタさん、仏生徒のデモに参加 「世界中が見守っている」
item.description:
Janis Laizans Clotaire Achi
[サンドニ（フランス） １３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Janis Laizans　Clotaire Achi

[サンドニ（フランス） １３日 ロイター] - スウェーデンの活動家グレタ・トゥンベリさんは１３日、パリ郊外の労働者が多く住む地区の高校前で、生徒らのデモに参加した。

パリなど各都市では午前中、生徒らが複数の学校の校門前に集まり、プラカードや拡声器を手にスローガンを叫んだ。この日はデモ行進も予定されている。

ジェフレ国民教育相はラジオ局フランス・アンテルに対し、約２００校が休校になったと述べた。一部は予定されているデモ行進の経路上にあるため、安全上の予防措置として休校にした可能性を示唆した。

グレタさんはフランスの生徒らにはもっと幅広い支援が寄せられるべきだと述べた。パリ北郊サンドニの高校前で記者団に「世界中の人々がこの動きを見守っていることを知ってほしい。基本的な権利を求める若者たちに私たちは勇気づけられている」と語った。

「学校の資金不足であれ、気候危機であれ、社会的不公正を巡る危機であれ、今こそ若者が立ち上がり、自分たちの未来を取り戻す時だ」と訴えた。

激しい議論を呼んでいる警察の対応について「極めて暴力的」だと批判した。当局が既存の体制を守り、若者の要求を無視していることの表れだと述べた。

item.title: Allies gave Ukraine no warning of impending missile attack, Zelenskiy says
item.description: Ukraine received no warning from Western partners before a Russian missile attack on its capital, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Tuesday, but President Donald Trump said Washington was still sharing intelligence even as he pressured Kyiv to halt attacks on Russian refineries.
item.dc:creator: Olena Harmash, Daniel Flynn
item.content:encoded: Ukraine received no warning from Western partners before a Russian missile attack on its capital, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Tuesday, but President Donald Trump said Washington was still sharing intelligence even as he pressured Kyiv to halt attacks on Russian refineries. Russia hit no Ukrainian energy targets overnight for the first time since Trump's surprise Sunday announcement of an "energy ceasefire", but hammered transport and logistics with ballistic missiles and drones. Reuters and other media have reported that US officials have threatened to cut off intelligence sharing and weapons sales to Ukraine unless it stops attacking Russian refineries. Kyiv relies heavily on US intelligence for early warnings of missile strikes, experts and officials say. Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Trump said Washington [USN:L1N45Z0QL TEXT:"continued to share intelligence with Ukraine"] and was working with both Kyiv and Moscow to end the war. "We are helping them, and we are sharing intel," he said. Trump was asked whether Russia had violated the ceasefire and answered: "I'll let you know about that later." Asked if Russia could use proceeds from the diesel deal to purchase more bombs, Trump sidestepped the question. "That's a diesel deal, not for us. That's being released into the world. That's not being released to us." Zelenskiy said Ukraine had not targeted Russian refineries since Trump's announcement on Sunday. He said Kyiv had not received the usual warning from allies of ballistic missile launches before a "particularly vile" attack on Kyiv overnight, in which five missiles hit civilian infrastructure. "Intelligence on Russian ballistic missile launches helps save lives," Zelenskiy said on X, "and this is one of the most critical issues." He stopped short of linking the lack of warning to any US threats. AIR RAID ALERTS SOUND IN KYIV ONLY AFTER BLASTS ARE HEARD Air alerts sounded in Kyiv on Monday night only after several explosions had already ripped through the city. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said Ukraine was still receiving US military intelligence and attributed the delay to the type of weapon Russia had used. As Ukraine fights a larger, richer and better-equipped enemy, Kyiv sees the strikes on Russian oil refineries as one of its few instruments to reduce Moscow's ability to fight. Yet Trump has repeatedly blamed Ukrainian attacks – which prompted Moscow to suspend [USN:L1N45Y0OS TEXT:"diesel exports"] – for a sharp rise in US fuel prices this year, a headache for his Republican Party ahead of congressional midterm elections in three weeks. Most analysts say the US war in Iran has had a far greater impact on the price rise. Russia had struck six Ukrainian energy sites on Monday. It was unclear whether Moscow had deliberately avoided energy infrastructure overnight and on Tuesday. A Kremlin spokesman, asked about the energy ceasefire, would only say that contacts were ongoing, but declined to provide any further details. In his nightly video address posted on X, Zelenskiy said he had sent proposals to US officials with a view to new meetings in coming days with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on ways to resolve the conflict. He said Ukraine supported Trump's announcement of an energy truce provided that Russia observed it. "We need to work for peace, we need to look for ways to do the proper actions. Ukraine is ready for meetings," he said. Earlier, Zelenskiy reiterated Ukraine's position, saying that Kyiv was ready for reciprocal steps to de-escalate, calling on partners to pressure Russia. A Ukrainian delegation held talks in the United States last week and people familiar with the meeting said Witkoff and Kushner [USN:L1N45Y0OS TEXT:"told"] them that a deal to allow Russian diesel exports was part of a bid to draw Russia back to negotiations. UKRAINE SAYS IT NOW HAS CARDS TO PLAY Russian strikes also killed four people in Ukraine's second city, Kharkiv, and dozens were wounded across the country, Ukrainian officials said. Fabian Hoffmann, a missile expert at the Norwegian Institute for Defence Studies, said Ukraine's European allies had "very limited" ability to replace US early-warning intelligence about Russian missile strikes. "Ukraine relies on the so-called Space-Based Infrared System which the US deploys – and the US system is really second to none and only the United States can provide that," he said. Sybiha said the US request to halt attacks on Russian refineries showed how Ukraine's position had strengthened, alluding to Trump's comment to Zelenskiy in a tense Oval Office meeting last year that "you don't have the cards". "In less than two years, we have gone from 'having no cards' to 'not playing your cards'. That is an achievement," Sybiha said.

item.title: Canada stocks rise as energy stocks gain
item.description: Canada's main stock index rose on Tuesday, lifted by energy shares, while a global semiconductor selloff amid renewed AI concerns drove investors into government bonds, helping stabilize yields.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index rose on Tuesday, lifted by energy shares, while a global semiconductor selloff amid renewed AI concerns drove investors into government bonds, helping stabilize yields. The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) closed up 0.90%, at 35,983.98. Energy shares (.SPTTEN) led gains despite lower oil prices Natural gas solution firm Enerflex (EFX.TO) jumped 14% after securing a major data-centre power project that lifted its behind-the-meter generation backlog above 1.75 GW through 2028 Materials (.GSPTTMT) fell 1.84% as silver dropped more than 1%, while gold was little changed Canada's 10-year government bond yield slipped to 3.871%, while the comparable US 10-year yield slipped to 5.2126% "There's perhaps a sense in the markets that bond yields have peaked short term and that seems to be driving the market more than anything else," said Matt Skipp, president at SW8 Asset Management TSX's financial stocks (.SPTTFS) added 1.4% after major US banks reported results. Investors have been grappling with inflation concerns lately tied to higher energy prices and rising government debt Global semiconductor shares were pressured by reports that Chinese memory-chip maker CXMT has made rapid advances, raising concerns that China is narrowing the technology gap Canada's technology sector nevertheless rose about 1.6%, helped by a 3% gain in Shopify (SHOP.TO) Markets are pricing in at least one more 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike by year-end, according to LSEG data In Canada, the TSX posted its biggest weekly gain in five weeks on Friday after [USN:L1N45V0EG TEXT:"soft jobs data"] reduced expectations of another Bank of Canada rate increase Markets are now seeing a 28% chance of a hike at this month's meeting

item.title: アジアでヘッジファンド投資拡大、「債券4割」の分散効果に疑問
item.description:
Summer Zhen Tom Westbrook
［香港 １３日 ロイター］ - アジアでヘッジファンド投資が拡大し...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
アジアでヘッジファンド投資拡大、「債券4割」の分散効果に疑問 10/13 19:29 配信

香港の金融街で2023年10月撮影 REUTERS/Tyrone Siu/File Photo

Summer Zhen　Tom Westbrook

［香港　１３日　ロイター］ - アジアでヘッジファンド投資が拡大している。年金基金やファミリーオフィスなどの投資家が、債券や株式の不安定な動きを受けてオルタナティブ（代替）資産に目を向けている。背景には、株式に６割、債券に４割を配分する「６０／４０」という投資の標準的なリスク管理戦略に疑問が生じていることがある。

ヘッジファンド・リサーチ（ＨＦＲ）のデータによると、２０２６年第２・四半期の世界のヘッジファンド運用資産は５兆６０００億ドル。四半期ベースで過去最大となる４０９０億ドルの伸びだった。運用成績も比較的堅調だ。ＨＦＲが算出する世界のヘッジファンド指数は年初来で７％上昇。２５年は１２．４％上昇した。

スイスのプライベートバンク、ＵＢＰによると、アジアで一任運用サービスを利用する顧客のうち、ヘッジファンドだけに投資するマンデート（運用委託）の比率は２４年末から３倍超に増えた。アジア一任運用部門責任者、パラス・グプタ氏は「米国債などの国債は、ここ数年で分散投資の手段としての信頼性が下がった」と述べ、その結果、ポートフォリオの中でヘッジファンドが果たせる役割が広がったと説明した。

戦略アドバイザーのマーシュのグローバル最高投資責任者（ＣＩＯ）、ニール・オサリバン氏によると、これまでヘッジファンドに投資していなかった一部機関投資家が、現在は約１０％の配分を望んでいる。特に、市場全体との相関が低いマルチストラテジー型ファンドが人気という。

マーシュ・アジアの投資責任者、アデリン・タン氏は、ウェルスマネジャーやファミリーオフィスのほか、日本の確定給付型年金などの大口機関投資家からも関心が寄せられていると話した。

ＪＰモルガン・プライベートバンクのアジア・オルタナティブ投資責任者、アルバート・ヤン氏は、ＡＩへの集中リスクが意識されていると指摘し、ヘッジファンドを変動に対応するための長期的な投資先とする例が増えていると述べた。

ただ、ヘッジファンド業界の中でも運用成績や資金の流れには大きなばらつきがある。ヤン氏は、ヘッジファンドへのシフトは伝統的なポートフォリオに取って代わるものではなく、新しい戦略と耐久力を補強する意味合いがあると述べた。

機動的で、株式市場の方向性に関係なくリターンを生み出せるマルチストラテジー型、マクロ型、クオンツ型などの運用会社が、特に大きな恩恵を受けている。
